title: 1 John 1:1–4
context: The apostle testifies to what was from the beginning: the Word of life, heard, seen, looked upon, and touched. That eternal life was with the Father and has been made manifest, so that hearers may have fellowship with the apostolic company—and that fellowship is with the Father and His Son Jesus Christ. He writes that joy may be complete.
text: 1 John 1:1–4 1 John The apostle testifies to what was from the beginning: the Word of life, heard, seen, looked upon, and touched. That eternal life was with the Father and has been made manifest, so that hearers may have fellowship with the apostolic company—and that fellowship is with the Father and His Son Jesus Christ. He writes that joy may be complete. That which was from the beginning, which we have heard, which we have seen with our eyes, which we looked upon and have touched with our hands, concerning the word of life— 1 John 1:1 the life was made manifest, and we have seen it, and testify to it and proclaim to you the eternal life, which was with the Father and was made manifest to us— 1 John 1:2 that which we have seen and heard we proclaim also to you, so that you too may have fellowship with us; and indeed our fellowship is with the Father and with his Son Jesus Christ. 1 John 1:3 And we are writing these things so that our joy may be complete. 1 John 1:4

title: 1 John 1:5–10
context: The message heard from Him is that God is light, and in Him is no darkness at all. Fellowship-talk while walking in darkness is a lie; walking in the light brings fellowship and cleansing by the Son’s blood. If we say we have no sin we deceive ourselves; if we confess, He is faithful and just to forgive and to cleanse. Claiming we have not sinned makes Him a liar.
text: 1 John 1:5–10 1 John The message heard from Him is that God is light, and in Him is no darkness at all. Fellowship-talk while walking in darkness is a lie; walking in the light brings fellowship and cleansing by the Son’s blood. If we say we have no sin we deceive ourselves; if we confess, He is faithful and just to forgive and to cleanse. Claiming we have not sinned makes Him a liar. This is the message we have heard from him and proclaim to you, that God is light, and in him is no darkness at all. 1 John 1:5 If we say we have fellowship with him while we walk in darkness, we lie and do not practice the truth. 1 John 1:6 But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship with one another, and the blood of Jesus his Son cleanses us from all sin. 1 John 1:7 If we say we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us. 1 John 1:8 If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness. 1 John 1:9 If we say we have not sinned, we make him a liar, and his word is not in us. 1 John 1:10

title: 1 John 2:1–6
context: John writes so that they may not sin—and if anyone does sin, they have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous, the propitiation for our sins and also for the sins of the whole world. Knowing him is proved by keeping his commandments; the one who claims to abide in him must walk as he walked.
text: 1 John 2:1–6 1 John John writes so that they may not sin—and if anyone does sin, they have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous, the propitiation for our sins and also for the sins of the whole world. Knowing him is proved by keeping his commandments; the one who claims to abide in him must walk as he walked. My little children, I am writing these things to you so that you may not sin. But if anyone does sin, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous. 1 John 2:1 He is the propitiation for our sins, and not for ours only but also for the sins of the whole world. 1 John 2:2 And by this we know that we have come to know him, if we keep his commandments. 1 John 2:3 Whoever says “I know him” but does not keep his commandments is a liar, and the truth is not in him, 1 John 2:4 but whoever keeps his word, in him truly the love of God is perfected. By this we may know that we are in him: 1 John 2:5 whoever says he abides in him ought to walk in the same way in which he walked. 1 John 2:6

title: 1 John 2:15–17
context: Do not love the world or the things in it. If anyone loves the world, the love of the Father is not in him. All that is in the world—desires of the flesh, desires of the eyes, pride of life—is not from the Father. The world is passing away with its desires; whoever does the will of God abides forever.
text: 1 John 2:15–17 1 John Do not love the world or the things in it. If anyone loves the world, the love of the Father is not in him. All that is in the world—desires of the flesh, desires of the eyes, pride of life—is not from the Father. The world is passing away with its desires; whoever does the will of God abides forever. Do not love the world or the things in the world. If anyone loves the world, the love of the Father is not in him. 1 John 2:15 For all that is in the world—the desires of the flesh and the desires of the eyes and pride of life—is not from the Father but is from the world. 1 John 2:16 And the world is passing away along with its desires, but whoever does the will of God abides forever. 1 John 2:17

title: 1 John 2:18–27
context: It is the last hour: antichrist was heard of, and many antichrists have come. They went out from us but were not of us; had they been, they would have continued. The anointing from the Holy One teaches. The liar denies that Jesus is the Christ, denying Father and Son. What was heard from the beginning must abide—and with it, the promise of eternal life. Abide in Him.
text: 1 John 2:18–27 1 John It is the last hour: antichrist was heard of, and many antichrists have come. They went out from us but were not of us; had they been, they would have continued. The anointing from the Holy One teaches. The liar denies that Jesus is the Christ, denying Father and Son. What was heard from the beginning must abide—and with it, the promise of eternal life. Abide in Him. Children, it is the last hour, and as you have heard that antichrist is coming, so now many antichrists have come. Therefore we know that it is the last hour. 1 John 2:18 They went out from us, but they were not of us; for if they had been of us, they would have continued with us. But they went out, that it might become plain that they all are not of us. 1 John 2:19 But you have been anointed by the Holy One, and you all have knowledge. 1 John 2:20 I write to you, not because you do not know the truth, but because you know it, and because no lie is of the truth. 1 John 2:21 Who is the liar but he who denies that Jesus is the Christ? This is the antichrist, he who denies the Father and the Son. 1 John 2:22 No one who denies the Son has the Father. Whoever confesses the Son has the Father also. 1 John 2:23 Let what you heard from the beginning abide in you. If what you heard from the beginning abides in you, then you too will abide in the Son and in the Father. 1 John 2:24 And this is the promise that he made to us—eternal life. 1 John 2:25 I write these things to you about those who are trying to deceive you. 1 John 2:26 But the anointing that you received from him abides in you, and you have no need that anyone should teach you. But as his anointing teaches you about everything, and is true, and is no lie—just as it has taught you, abide in him. 1 John 2:27

title: 1 John 2:7–14
context: The commandment is old—from the beginning—and new, true in Him and in them, because the darkness is passing and the true light is shining. Love of the brother abides in the light; hatred walks blind. John writes to children, fathers, and young men: sins forgiven, the One from the beginning known, the evil one overcome, the Father known, the word abiding.
text: 1 John 2:7–14 1 John The commandment is old—from the beginning—and new, true in Him and in them, because the darkness is passing and the true light is shining. Love of the brother abides in the light; hatred walks blind. John writes to children, fathers, and young men: sins forgiven, the One from the beginning known, the evil one overcome, the Father known, the word abiding. Beloved, I am writing you no new commandment, but an old commandment that you had from the beginning. The old commandment is the word that you have heard. 1 John 2:7 At the same time, it is a new commandment that I am writing to you, which is true in him and in you, because the darkness is passing away and the true light is already shining. 1 John 2:8 Whoever says he is in the light and hates his brother is still in darkness. 1 John 2:9 Whoever loves his brother abides in the light, and in him there is no cause for stumbling. 1 John 2:10 But whoever hates his brother is in the darkness and walks in the darkness, and does not know where he is going, because the darkness has blinded his eyes. 1 John 2:11 I am writing to you, little children, because your sins are forgiven for his name's sake. 1 John 2:12 I am writing to you, fathers, because you know him who is from the beginning. I am writing to you, young men, because you have overcome the evil one. I write to you, children, because you know the Father. 1 John 2:13 I write to you, fathers, because you know him who is from the beginning. I write to you, young men, because you are strong, and the word of God abides in you, and you have overcome the evil one. 1 John 2:14

title: 1 John 3:1–10
context: See what kind of love the Father has given: we are called children of God, and so we are. What we will be has not appeared; we shall be like Him when He appears. Everyone who hopes in Him purifies himself. No one who abides in Him keeps on sinning; no one born of God makes a practice of sinning, because God’s seed abides. By this the children of God and of the devil are evident.
text: 1 John 3:1–10 1 John See what kind of love the Father has given: we are called children of God, and so we are. What we will be has not appeared; we shall be like Him when He appears. Everyone who hopes in Him purifies himself. No one who abides in Him keeps on sinning; no one born of God makes a practice of sinning, because God’s seed abides. By this the children of God and of the devil are evident. See what kind of love the Father has given to us, that we should be called children of God; and so we are. The reason why the world does not know us is that it did not know him. 1 John 3:1 Beloved, we are God's children now, and what we will be has not yet appeared; but we know that when he appears we shall be like him, because we shall see him as he is. 1 John 3:2 And everyone who thus hopes in him purifies himself as he is pure. 1 John 3:3 Everyone who makes a practice of sinning also practices lawlessness; sin is lawlessness. 1 John 3:4 You know that he appeared in order to take away sins, and in him there is no sin. 1 John 3:5 No one who abides in him keeps on sinning; no one who keeps on sinning has either seen him or known him. 1 John 3:6 Little children, let no one deceive you. Whoever practices righteousness is righteous, as he is righteous. 1 John 3:7 Whoever makes a practice of sinning is of the devil, for the devil has been sinning from the beginning. The reason the Son of God appeared was to destroy the works of the devil. 1 John 3:8 No one born of God makes a practice of sinning, for God's seed abides in him; and he cannot keep on sinning, because he has been born of God. 1 John 3:9 By this it is evident who are the children of God, and who are the children of the devil: whoever does not practice righteousness is not of God, nor is the one who does not love his brother. 1 John 3:10

title: 1 John 3:11–24
context: The message from the beginning is that we should love one another—not as Cain. Love of the brothers is how we know we have passed from death to life. He laid down His life for us; we ought to lay down ours, and open our goods to the brother in need. Love in deed and truth reassures the heart. The commandment is to believe in the name of His Son and love one another. We know He abides by the Spirit He has given.
text: 1 John 3:11–24 1 John The message from the beginning is that we should love one another—not as Cain. Love of the brothers is how we know we have passed from death to life. He laid down His life for us; we ought to lay down ours, and open our goods to the brother in need. Love in deed and truth reassures the heart. The commandment is to believe in the name of His Son and love one another. We know He abides by the Spirit He has given. For this is the message that you have heard from the beginning, that we should love one another. 1 John 3:11 We should not be like Cain, who was of the evil one and murdered his brother. And why did he murder him? Because his own deeds were evil and his brother's righteous. 1 John 3:12 Do not be surprised, brothers, that the world hates you. 1 John 3:13 We know that we have passed out of death into life, because we love the brothers. Whoever does not love abides in death. 1 John 3:14 Everyone who hates his brother is a murderer, and you know that no murderer has eternal life abiding in him. 1 John 3:15 By this we know love, that he laid down his life for us, and we ought to lay down our lives for the brothers. 1 John 3:16 But if anyone has the world's goods and sees his brother in need, yet closes his heart against him, how does God's love abide in him? 1 John 3:17 Little children, let us not love in word or talk but in deed and in truth. 1 John 3:18 By this we shall know that we are of the truth and reassure our heart before him; 1 John 3:19 for whenever our heart condemns us, God is greater than our heart, and he knows everything. 1 John 3:20 Beloved, if our heart does not condemn us, we have confidence before God; 1 John 3:21 and whatever we ask we receive from him, because we keep his commandments and do what pleases him. 1 John 3:22 And this is his commandment, that we believe in the name of his Son Jesus Christ and love one another, just as he has commanded us. 1 John 3:23 Whoever keeps his commandments abides in God, and God in him. And by this we know that he abides in us, by the Spirit whom he has given us. 1 John 3:24

title: 1 John 4:1–6
context: Do not believe every spirit; test the spirits, for many false prophets have gone out. Every spirit that confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is from God; the one that does not is the spirit of antichrist already in the world. The children of God have overcome them, because He who is in them is greater. The world listens to its own; whoever knows God listens to the apostolic testimony.
text: 1 John 4:1–6 1 John Do not believe every spirit; test the spirits, for many false prophets have gone out. Every spirit that confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is from God; the one that does not is the spirit of antichrist already in the world. The children of God have overcome them, because He who is in them is greater. The world listens to its own; whoever knows God listens to the apostolic testimony. Beloved, do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits to see whether they are from God, for many false prophets have gone out into the world. 1 John 4:1 By this you know the Spirit of God: every spirit that confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is from God, 1 John 4:2 and every spirit that does not confess Jesus is not from God. This is the spirit of the antichrist, which you heard was coming and now is in the world already. 1 John 4:3 Little children, you are from God and have overcome them, for he who is in you is greater than he who is in the world. 1 John 4:4 They are from the world; therefore they speak from the world, and the world listens to them. 1 John 4:5 We are from God. Whoever knows God listens to us; whoever is not from God does not listen to us. By this we know the Spirit of truth and the spirit of error. 1 John 4:6

title: 1 John 4:7–21
context: Beloved, let us love one another: love is from God, and God is love. His love was made manifest in sending His only Son into the world as the propitiation for our sins, the Savior of the world. We love because He first loved us; whoever loves God must also love his brother. Fear is cast out where love is perfected.
text: 1 John 4:7–21 1 John Beloved, let us love one another: love is from God, and God is love. His love was made manifest in sending His only Son into the world as the propitiation for our sins, the Savior of the world. We love because He first loved us; whoever loves God must also love his brother. Fear is cast out where love is perfected. Beloved, let us love one another, for love is from God, and whoever loves has been born of God and knows God. 1 John 4:7 Anyone who does not love does not know God, because God is love. 1 John 4:8 In this the love of God was made manifest among us, that God sent his only Son into the world, so that we might live through him. 1 John 4:9 In this is love, not that we have loved God but that he loved us and sent his Son to be the propitiation for our sins. 1 John 4:10 Beloved, if God so loved us, we also ought to love one another. 1 John 4:11 No one has ever seen God; if we love one another, God abides in us and his love is perfected in us. 1 John 4:12 By this we know that we abide in him and he in us, because he has given us of his Spirit. 1 John 4:13 And we have seen and testify that the Father has sent his Son to be the Savior of the world. 1 John 4:14 Whoever confesses that Jesus is the Son of God, God abides in him, and he in God. 1 John 4:15 So we have come to know and to believe the love that God has for us. God is love, and whoever abides in love abides in God, and God abides in him. 1 John 4:16 By this is love perfected with us, so that we may have confidence for the day of judgment, because as he is so also are we in this world. 1 John 4:17 There is no fear in love, but perfect love casts out fear. For fear has to do with punishment, and whoever fears has not been perfected in love. 1 John 4:18 We love because he first loved us. 1 John 4:19 If anyone says, “I love God,” and hates his brother, he is a liar; for he who does not love his brother whom he has seen cannot love God whom he has not seen. 1 John 4:20 And this commandment we have from him: whoever loves God must also love his brother. 1 John 4:21

title: 1 John 5:1–12
context: Everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ has been born of God, and love of the Father includes love of those born of Him. His commandments are not burdensome; faith is the victory that overcomes the world. Jesus Christ came by water and blood; the Spirit testifies. The testimony is that God gave us eternal life, and this life is in His Son: whoever has the Son has life.
text: 1 John 5:1–12 1 John Everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ has been born of God, and love of the Father includes love of those born of Him. His commandments are not burdensome; faith is the victory that overcomes the world. Jesus Christ came by water and blood; the Spirit testifies. The testimony is that God gave us eternal life, and this life is in His Son: whoever has the Son has life. Everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ has been born of God, and everyone who loves the Father loves whoever has been born of him. 1 John 5:1 By this we know that we love the children of God, when we love God and obey his commandments. 1 John 5:2 For this is the love of God, that we keep his commandments. And his commandments are not burdensome. 1 John 5:3 For everyone who has been born of God overcomes the world. And this is the victory that has overcome the world—our faith. 1 John 5:4 Who is it that overcomes the world except the one who believes that Jesus is the Son of God? 1 John 5:5 This is he who came by water and blood—Jesus Christ; not by the water only but by the water and the blood. And the Spirit is the one who testifies, because the Spirit is the truth. 1 John 5:6 For there are three that testify: 1 John 5:7 the Spirit and the water and the blood; and these three agree. 1 John 5:8 If we receive the testimony of men, the testimony of God is greater, for this is the testimony of God that he has borne concerning his Son. 1 John 5:9 Whoever believes in the Son of God has the testimony in himself. Whoever does not believe God has made him a liar, because he has not believed in the testimony that God has borne concerning his Son. 1 John 5:10 And this is the testimony, that God gave us eternal life, and this life is in his Son. 1 John 5:11 Whoever has the Son has life; whoever does not have the Son of God does not have life. 1 John 5:12

title: 1 John 5:13–21
context: John writes to those who believe in the name of the Son of God, that they may know they have eternal life. Confidence in prayer according to His will; a brother sinning not unto death may be asked for; there is sin that leads to death. The one born of God does not keep on sinning; we are from God, the world lies in the evil one. The Son has come and given understanding: He is the true God and eternal life. Keep yourselves from idols.
text: 1 John 5:13–21 1 John John writes to those who believe in the name of the Son of God, that they may know they have eternal life. Confidence in prayer according to His will; a brother sinning not unto death may be asked for; there is sin that leads to death. The one born of God does not keep on sinning; we are from God, the world lies in the evil one. The Son has come and given understanding: He is the true God and eternal life. Keep yourselves from idols. I write these things to you who believe in the name of the Son of God, that you may know that you have eternal life. 1 John 5:13 And this is the confidence that we have toward him, that if we ask anything according to his will he hears us. 1 John 5:14 And if we know that he hears us in whatever we ask, we know that we have the requests that we have asked of him. 1 John 5:15 If anyone sees his brother committing a sin not leading to death, he shall ask, and God will give him life—to those who commit sins that do not lead to death. There is sin that leads to death; I do not say that one should pray for that. 1 John 5:16 All wrongdoing is sin, but there is sin that does not lead to death. 1 John 5:17 We know that everyone who has been born of God does not keep on sinning, but he who was born of God protects him, and the evil one does not touch him. 1 John 5:18 We know that we are from God, and the whole world lies in the power of the evil one. 1 John 5:19 And we know that the Son of God has come and has given us understanding, so that we may know him who is true; and we are in him who is true, in his Son Jesus Christ. He is the true God and eternal life. 1 John 5:20 Little children, keep yourselves from idols. 1 John 5:21

title: 1 Timothy 1:1–2
context: Paul greets Timothy as his true child in the faith, naming himself an apostle by command of God our Savior and of Christ Jesus our hope. The blessing adds mercy to grace and peace—a tender word for a young minister standing in a hard charge.
text: 1 Timothy 1:1–2 1 Timothy Paul greets Timothy as his true child in the faith, naming himself an apostle by command of God our Savior and of Christ Jesus our hope. The blessing adds mercy to grace and peace—a tender word for a young minister standing in a hard charge. Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by command of God our Savior and of Christ Jesus our hope, 1 Timothy 1:1 To Timothy, my true child in the faith: Grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord. 1 Timothy 1:2

title: 1 Timothy 1:12–17
context: Paul thanks Christ Jesus who strengthened him and appointed him to service, though he had been a blasphemer, persecutor, and insolent opponent. Mercy met his ignorant unbelief; grace overflowed with faith and love; and the trustworthy saying is that Christ came to save sinners—Paul the foremost, a pattern of perfect patience for those who would believe—crowned with doxology to the King of the ages.
text: 1 Timothy 1:12–17 1 Timothy Paul thanks Christ Jesus who strengthened him and appointed him to service, though he had been a blasphemer, persecutor, and insolent opponent. Mercy met his ignorant unbelief; grace overflowed with faith and love; and the trustworthy saying is that Christ came to save sinners—Paul the foremost, a pattern of perfect patience for those who would believe—crowned with doxology to the King of the ages. I thank him who has given me strength, Christ Jesus our Lord, because he judged me faithful, appointing me to his service, 1 Timothy 1:12 though formerly I was a blasphemer, persecutor, and insolent opponent. But I received mercy because I had acted ignorantly in unbelief, 1 Timothy 1:13 and the grace of our Lord overflowed for me with the faith and love that are in Christ Jesus. 1 Timothy 1:14 The saying is trustworthy and deserving of full acceptance, that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, of whom I am the foremost. 1 Timothy 1:15 But I received mercy for this reason, that in me, as the foremost, Jesus Christ might display his perfect patience as an example to those who were to believe in him for eternal life. 1 Timothy 1:16 To the King of the ages, immortal, invisible, the only God, be honor and glory forever and ever. Amen. 1 Timothy 1:17

title: 1 Timothy 1:18–20
context: Paul entrusts this charge to Timothy in line with earlier prophecies, that he may wage the good warfare, holding faith and a good conscience. Some have shipwrecked that faith; Hymenaeus and Alexander are named, handed over to Satan that they may learn not to blaspheme.
text: 1 Timothy 1:18–20 1 Timothy Paul entrusts this charge to Timothy in line with earlier prophecies, that he may wage the good warfare, holding faith and a good conscience. Some have shipwrecked that faith; Hymenaeus and Alexander are named, handed over to Satan that they may learn not to blaspheme. This charge I entrust to you, Timothy, my child, in accordance with the prophecies previously made about you, that by them you may wage the good warfare, 1 Timothy 1:18 holding faith and a good conscience. By rejecting this, some have made shipwreck of their faith, 1 Timothy 1:19 among whom are Hymenaeus and Alexander, whom I have handed over to Satan that they may learn not to blaspheme. 1 Timothy 1:20

title: 1 Timothy 1:3–11
context: Paul reminds Timothy why he remained at Ephesus: to charge certain persons not to teach a different doctrine or lose themselves in myths and endless genealogies. The aim of the charge is love from a pure heart, a good conscience, and a sincere faith; the law is good when used lawfully, and sound doctrine accords with the gospel of the blessed God’s glory.
text: 1 Timothy 1:3–11 1 Timothy Paul reminds Timothy why he remained at Ephesus: to charge certain persons not to teach a different doctrine or lose themselves in myths and endless genealogies. The aim of the charge is love from a pure heart, a good conscience, and a sincere faith; the law is good when used lawfully, and sound doctrine accords with the gospel of the blessed God’s glory. As I urged you when I was going to Macedonia, remain at Ephesus so that you may charge certain persons not to teach any different doctrine, 1 Timothy 1:3 nor to devote themselves to myths and endless genealogies, which promote speculations rather than the stewardship from God that is by faith. 1 Timothy 1:4 The aim of our charge is love that issues from a pure heart and a good conscience and a sincere faith. 1 Timothy 1:5 Certain persons, by swerving from these, have wandered away into vain discussion, 1 Timothy 1:6 desiring to be teachers of the law, without understanding either what they are saying or the things about which they make confident assertions. 1 Timothy 1:7 Now we know that the law is good, if one uses it lawfully, 1 Timothy 1:8 understanding this, that the law is not laid down for the just but for the lawless and disobedient, for the ungodly and sinners, for the unholy and profane, for those who strike their fathers and mothers, for murderers, 1 Timothy 1:9 the sexually immoral, men who practice homosexuality, enslavers, liars, perjurers, and whatever else is contrary to sound doctrine, 1 Timothy 1:10 in accordance with the gospel of the glory of the blessed God with which I have been entrusted. 1 Timothy 1:11

title: 1 Timothy 2:1–7
context: Paul turns from charge to Timothy toward the church’s public life: first of all, pray for all people, including kings, so that a quiet, godly life may flourish. The reason is soteriological and Christological: God our Savior desires all people to be saved; there is one mediator, the man Christ Jesus, who gave himself as a ransom for all—the testimony Paul was appointed to preach among the Gentiles.
text: 1 Timothy 2:1–7 1 Timothy Paul turns from charge to Timothy toward the church’s public life: first of all, pray for all people, including kings, so that a quiet, godly life may flourish. The reason is soteriological and Christological: God our Savior desires all people to be saved; there is one mediator, the man Christ Jesus, who gave himself as a ransom for all—the testimony Paul was appointed to preach among the Gentiles. First of all, then, I urge that supplications, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgivings be made for all people, 1 Timothy 2:1 for kings and all who are in high positions, that we may lead a peaceful and quiet life, godly and dignified in every way. 1 Timothy 2:2 This is good, and it is pleasing in the sight of God our Savior, 1 Timothy 2:3 who desires all people to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth. 1 Timothy 2:4 For there is one God, and there is one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus, 1 Timothy 2:5 who gave himself as a ransom for all, which is the testimony given at the proper time. 1 Timothy 2:6 For this I was appointed a preacher and an apostle (I am telling the truth, I am not lying), a teacher of the Gentiles in faith and truth. 1 Timothy 2:7

title: 1 Timothy 2:8–15
context: From prayer for all people Paul turns to how the gathered church should look: men praying in every place without anger or quarreling; women adorned with modesty, self-control, and good works rather than display. A woman is to learn quietly; Paul does not permit her to teach or exercise authority over a man, grounding the charge in Adam formed first and Eve deceived, then adding the hard pastoral word that she will be saved through childbearing if they continue in faith, love, and holiness with self-control.
text: 1 Timothy 2:8–15 1 Timothy From prayer for all people Paul turns to how the gathered church should look: men praying in every place without anger or quarreling; women adorned with modesty, self-control, and good works rather than display. A woman is to learn quietly; Paul does not permit her to teach or exercise authority over a man, grounding the charge in Adam formed first and Eve deceived, then adding the hard pastoral word that she will be saved through childbearing if they continue in faith, love, and holiness with self-control. I desire then that in every place the men should pray, lifting holy hands without anger or quarreling; 1 Timothy 2:8 likewise also that women should adorn themselves in respectable apparel, with modesty and self-control, not with braided hair and gold or pearls or costly attire, 1 Timothy 2:9 but with what is proper for women who profess godliness—with good works. 1 Timothy 2:10 Let a woman learn quietly with all submissiveness. 1 Timothy 2:11 I do not permit a woman to teach or to exercise authority over a man; rather, she is to remain quiet. 1 Timothy 2:12 For Adam was formed first, then Eve; 1 Timothy 2:13 and Adam was not deceived, but the woman was deceived and became a transgressor. 1 Timothy 2:14 Yet she will be saved through childbearing—if they continue in faith and love and holiness, with self-control. 1 Timothy 2:15

title: 1 Timothy 3:1–7
context: Paul turns from household prayer to household office: the saying is trustworthy that aspiring to overseer is desiring a noble task. The overseer must be above reproach—a one-woman man, sober, hospitable, able to teach, not violent or greedy—managing his own house well, not a recent convert, and well thought of by outsiders, lest he fall into the devil’s snare.
text: 1 Timothy 3:1–7 1 Timothy Paul turns from household prayer to household office: the saying is trustworthy that aspiring to overseer is desiring a noble task. The overseer must be above reproach—a one-woman man, sober, hospitable, able to teach, not violent or greedy—managing his own house well, not a recent convert, and well thought of by outsiders, lest he fall into the devil’s snare. The saying is trustworthy: If anyone aspires to the office of overseer, he desires a noble task. 1 Timothy 3:1 Therefore an overseer must be above reproach, the husband of one wife, sober-minded, self-controlled, respectable, hospitable, able to teach, 1 Timothy 3:2 not a drunkard, not violent but gentle, not quarrelsome, not a lover of money. 1 Timothy 3:3 He must manage his own household well, with all dignity keeping his children submissive, 1 Timothy 3:4 for if someone does not know how to manage his own household, how will he care for God’s church? 1 Timothy 3:5 He must not be a recent convert, or he may become puffed up with conceit and fall into the condemnation of the devil. 1 Timothy 3:6 Moreover, he must be well thought of by outsiders, so that he may not fall into disgrace, into a snare of the devil. 1 Timothy 3:7

title: 1 Timothy 3:14–16
context: Paul hopes to come soon, yet writes so Timothy will know how one ought to behave in God’s household—the church of the living God, a pillar and buttress of the truth. The confessed mystery of godliness is Christ: manifested in the flesh, vindicated by the Spirit, seen by angels, proclaimed among the nations, believed on in the world, taken up in glory.
text: 1 Timothy 3:14–16 1 Timothy Paul hopes to come soon, yet writes so Timothy will know how one ought to behave in God’s household—the church of the living God, a pillar and buttress of the truth. The confessed mystery of godliness is Christ: manifested in the flesh, vindicated by the Spirit, seen by angels, proclaimed among the nations, believed on in the world, taken up in glory. I hope to come to you soon, but I am writing these things to you so that, 1 Timothy 3:14 if I delay, you may know how one ought to behave in the household of God, which is the church of the living God, a pillar and buttress of the truth. 1 Timothy 3:15 Great indeed, we confess, is the mystery of godliness: He was manifested in the flesh, vindicated by the Spirit, seen by angels, proclaimed among the nations, believed on in the world, taken up in glory. 1 Timothy 3:16

title: 1 Timothy 3:8–13
context: Deacons likewise must be dignified, truthful in speech, free of wine and dishonest gain, holding the mystery of the faith with a clear conscience. They are tested first, then they serve. Their wives (or the women) must be dignified and faithful; deacons too are one-woman men who manage households well. Those who serve well gain a good standing and great confidence in the faith that is in Christ Jesus.
text: 1 Timothy 3:8–13 1 Timothy Deacons likewise must be dignified, truthful in speech, free of wine and dishonest gain, holding the mystery of the faith with a clear conscience. They are tested first, then they serve. Their wives (or the women) must be dignified and faithful; deacons too are one-woman men who manage households well. Those who serve well gain a good standing and great confidence in the faith that is in Christ Jesus. Deacons likewise must be dignified, not double-tongued, not addicted to much wine, not greedy for dishonest gain. 1 Timothy 3:8 They must hold the mystery of the faith with a clear conscience. 1 Timothy 3:9 And let them also be tested first; then let them serve as deacons if they prove themselves blameless. 1 Timothy 3:10 Their wives likewise must be dignified, not slanderers, but sober-minded, faithful in all things. 1 Timothy 3:11 Let deacons each be the husband of one wife, managing their children and their own households well. 1 Timothy 3:12 For those who serve well as deacons gain a good standing for themselves and also great confidence in the faith that is in Christ Jesus. 1 Timothy 3:13

title: 1 Timothy 4:1–5
context: The Spirit expressly says that in later times some will depart from the faith, giving themselves to deceitful spirits and teachings of demons, through insincere liars with seared consciences. They forbid marriage and require abstinence from foods God created to be received with thanksgiving by those who believe and know the truth. Everything created by God is good, and nothing is to be rejected if received with thanksgiving, for it is made holy by the word of God and prayer.
text: 1 Timothy 4:1–5 1 Timothy The Spirit expressly says that in later times some will depart from the faith, giving themselves to deceitful spirits and teachings of demons, through insincere liars with seared consciences. They forbid marriage and require abstinence from foods God created to be received with thanksgiving by those who believe and know the truth. Everything created by God is good, and nothing is to be rejected if received with thanksgiving, for it is made holy by the word of God and prayer. Now the Spirit expressly says that in later times some will depart from the faith by devoting themselves to deceitful spirits and teachings of demons, 1 Timothy 4:1 through the insincerity of liars whose consciences are seared, 1 Timothy 4:2 who forbid marriage and require abstinence from foods that God created to be received with thanksgiving by those who believe and know the truth. 1 Timothy 4:3 For everything created by God is good, and nothing is to be rejected if it is received with thanksgiving, 1 Timothy 4:4 for it is made holy by the word of God and prayer. 1 Timothy 4:5

title: 1 Timothy 4:6–16
context: Timothy will be a good servant of Christ Jesus if he puts these things before the brothers, trained in the words of the faith and good doctrine. He is to refuse irreverent myths, train for godliness, and set his hope on the living God, the Savior of all people, especially of those who believe. He must command and teach, be an example despite youth, devote himself to public reading, exhortation, and teaching, not neglect the gift given by prophecy with the elders’ hands, practice these things, and watch himself and the teaching—so saving himself and his hearers.
text: 1 Timothy 4:6–16 1 Timothy Timothy will be a good servant of Christ Jesus if he puts these things before the brothers, trained in the words of the faith and good doctrine. He is to refuse irreverent myths, train for godliness, and set his hope on the living God, the Savior of all people, especially of those who believe. He must command and teach, be an example despite youth, devote himself to public reading, exhortation, and teaching, not neglect the gift given by prophecy with the elders’ hands, practice these things, and watch himself and the teaching—so saving himself and his hearers. If you put these things before the brothers, you will be a good servant of Christ Jesus, being trained in the words of the faith and of the good doctrine that you have followed. 1 Timothy 4:6 Have nothing to do with irreverent, silly myths. Rather train yourself for godliness; 1 Timothy 4:7 for while bodily training is of some value, godliness is of value in every way, as it holds promise for the present life and also for the life to come. 1 Timothy 4:8 The saying is trustworthy and deserving of full acceptance. 1 Timothy 4:9 For to this end we toil and strive, because we have our hope set on the living God, who is the Savior of all people, especially of those who believe. 1 Timothy 4:10 Command and teach these things. 1 Timothy 4:11 Let no one despise you for your youth, but set the believers an example in speech, in conduct, in love, in faith, in purity. 1 Timothy 4:12 Until I come, devote yourself to the public reading of Scripture, to exhortation, to teaching. 1 Timothy 4:13 Do not neglect the gift you have, which was given you by prophecy when the council of elders laid their hands on you. 1 Timothy 4:14 Practice these things, immerse yourself in them, so that all may see your progress. 1 Timothy 4:15 Keep a close watch on yourself and on the teaching. Persist in this, for by so doing you will save both yourself and your hearers. 1 Timothy 4:16

title: 1 Timothy 5:1–8
context: Paul trains Timothy to treat the congregation as a household: older men as fathers, younger as brothers, women as mothers and sisters in all purity. He then honors true widows, insists that families provide first, and warns that neglect of one's own house is a denial of the faith.
text: 1 Timothy 5:1–8 1 Timothy Paul trains Timothy to treat the congregation as a household: older men as fathers, younger as brothers, women as mothers and sisters in all purity. He then honors true widows, insists that families provide first, and warns that neglect of one's own house is a denial of the faith. Do not rebuke an older man but encourage him as you would a father, younger men as brothers, 1 Timothy 5:1 older women as mothers, younger women as sisters, in all purity. 1 Timothy 5:2 Honor widows who are truly widows. 1 Timothy 5:3 But if a widow has children or grandchildren, let them first learn to show godliness to their own household and to make some return to their parents, for this is pleasing in the sight of God. 1 Timothy 5:4 She who is truly a widow, left all alone, has set her hope on God and continues in supplications and prayers night and day, 1 Timothy 5:5 but she who is self-indulgent is dead even while she lives. 1 Timothy 5:6 Command these things as well, so that they may be without reproach. 1 Timothy 5:7 But if anyone does not provide for his relatives, and especially for members of his household, he has denied the faith and is worse than an unbeliever. 1 Timothy 5:8

title: 1 Timothy 5:17–25
context: Paul moves from enrolled widows to elders: those who rule well, especially in preaching and teaching, are worthy of double honor, for Scripture forbids muzzling the ox and says the laborer deserves his wages. Charges need two or three witnesses; persistent sin is rebuked publicly; Timothy must not prejudge, not lay hands hastily, and remember that both sins and good works will come to light.
text: 1 Timothy 5:17–25 1 Timothy Paul moves from enrolled widows to elders: those who rule well, especially in preaching and teaching, are worthy of double honor, for Scripture forbids muzzling the ox and says the laborer deserves his wages. Charges need two or three witnesses; persistent sin is rebuked publicly; Timothy must not prejudge, not lay hands hastily, and remember that both sins and good works will come to light. Let the elders who rule well be considered worthy of double honor, especially those who labor in preaching and teaching. 1 Timothy 5:17 For the Scripture says, "You shall not muzzle an ox when it treads out the grain," and, "The laborer deserves his wages." 1 Timothy 5:18 Do not admit a charge against an elder except on the evidence of two or three witnesses. 1 Timothy 5:19 As for those who persist in sin, rebuke them in the presence of all, so that the rest may stand in fear. 1 Timothy 5:20 In the presence of God and of Christ Jesus and of the elect angels I charge you to keep these rules without prejudging, doing nothing from partiality. 1 Timothy 5:21 Do not be hasty in the laying on of hands, nor take part in the sins of others; keep yourself pure. 1 Timothy 5:22 No longer drink only water, but use a little wine for the sake of your stomach and your frequent ailments. 1 Timothy 5:23 The sins of some people are conspicuous, going before them to judgment, but the sins of others appear later. 1 Timothy 5:24 So also good works are conspicuous, and even those that are not cannot remain hidden. 1 Timothy 5:25

title: 1 Timothy 5:9–16
context: Paul sets an enrollment for older widows of proven life—one-husband faithfulness, hospitality, care for the afflicted—while refusing younger widows whose passions may pull them from a pledged service. He would have them marry and manage homes, and he keeps the church's burden for those who are truly widows.
text: 1 Timothy 5:9–16 1 Timothy Paul sets an enrollment for older widows of proven life—one-husband faithfulness, hospitality, care for the afflicted—while refusing younger widows whose passions may pull them from a pledged service. He would have them marry and manage homes, and he keeps the church's burden for those who are truly widows. Let a widow be enrolled if she is not less than sixty years of age, having been the wife of one husband, 1 Timothy 5:9 and having a reputation for good works: if she has brought up children, has shown hospitality, has washed the feet of the saints, has cared for the afflicted, and has devoted herself to every good work. 1 Timothy 5:10 But refuse to enroll younger widows, for when their passions draw them away from Christ, they desire to marry 1 Timothy 5:11 and so incur condemnation for having abandoned their former faith. 1 Timothy 5:12 Besides that, they learn to be idlers, going about from house to house, and not only idlers, but also gossips and busybodies, saying what they should not. 1 Timothy 5:13 So I would have younger widows marry, bear children, manage their households, and give the adversary no occasion for slander. 1 Timothy 5:14 For some have already strayed after Satan. 1 Timothy 5:15 If any believing woman has relatives who are widows, let her care for them. Let the church not be burdened, so that it may care for those who are truly widows. 1 Timothy 5:16

title: 1 Timothy 6:1–2
context: Paul addresses believers already living under a first-century yoke: honor masters so that the name of God and the teaching are not reviled. Those with believing masters must not despise them as mere equals; they should serve all the better, because those who benefit are believers and beloved. Teach and urge these things.
text: 1 Timothy 6:1–2 1 Timothy Paul addresses believers already living under a first-century yoke: honor masters so that the name of God and the teaching are not reviled. Those with believing masters must not despise them as mere equals; they should serve all the better, because those who benefit are believers and beloved. Teach and urge these things. Let all who are under a yoke as bondservants regard their own masters as worthy of all honor, so that the name of God and the teaching may not be reviled. 1 Timothy 6:1 Those who have believing masters must not be disrespectful on the ground that they are brothers; rather they must serve all the better since those who benefit by their good service are believers and beloved. Teach and urge these things. 1 Timothy 6:2

title: 1 Timothy 6:11–16
context: Timothy, addressed as a man of God, must flee greed and pursue righteousness, godliness, faith, love, steadfastness, and gentleness. He is to fight the good fight of the faith, take hold of the eternal life to which he was called, and keep the commandment unstained until Christ appears: before God who gives life to all things, and before the blessed and only Sovereign.
text: 1 Timothy 6:11–16 1 Timothy Timothy, addressed as a man of God, must flee greed and pursue righteousness, godliness, faith, love, steadfastness, and gentleness. He is to fight the good fight of the faith, take hold of the eternal life to which he was called, and keep the commandment unstained until Christ appears: before God who gives life to all things, and before the blessed and only Sovereign. But as for you, O man of God, flee these things. Pursue righteousness, godliness, faith, love, steadfastness, gentleness. 1 Timothy 6:11 Fight the good fight of the faith. Take hold of the eternal life to which you were called and about which you made the good confession in the presence of many witnesses. 1 Timothy 6:12 I charge you in the presence of God, who gives life to all things, and of Christ Jesus, who in his testimony before Pontius Pilate made the good confession, 1 Timothy 6:13 to keep the commandment unstained and free from reproach until the appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ, 1 Timothy 6:14 which he will display at the proper time—he who is the blessed and only Sovereign, the King of kings and Lord of lords, 1 Timothy 6:15 who alone has immortality, who dwells in unapproachable light, whom no one has ever seen or can see. To him be honor and eternal dominion. Amen. 1 Timothy 6:16

title: 1 Timothy 6:17–21
context: The rich in this present age must not be haughty or set their hope on uncertain riches, but on God who richly provides everything to enjoy. They are to be rich in good works, generous, storing a foundation for the future, and so take hold of what is truly life. Timothy must guard the entrusted deposit, avoid irreverent babble falsely called knowledge, and remember that some have already swerved from the faith. Grace be with you.
text: 1 Timothy 6:17–21 1 Timothy The rich in this present age must not be haughty or set their hope on uncertain riches, but on God who richly provides everything to enjoy. They are to be rich in good works, generous, storing a foundation for the future, and so take hold of what is truly life. Timothy must guard the entrusted deposit, avoid irreverent babble falsely called knowledge, and remember that some have already swerved from the faith. Grace be with you. As for the rich in this present age, charge them not to be haughty, nor to set their hopes on the uncertainty of riches, but on God, who richly provides us with everything to enjoy. 1 Timothy 6:17 They are to do good, to be rich in good works, to be generous and ready to share, 1 Timothy 6:18 thus storing up treasure for themselves as a good foundation for the future, so that they may take hold of that which is truly life. 1 Timothy 6:19 O Timothy, guard the deposit entrusted to you. Avoid the irreverent babble and contradictions of what is falsely called "knowledge," 1 Timothy 6:20 for by professing it some have swerved from the faith. Grace be with you. 1 Timothy 6:21

title: 1 Timothy 6:3–10
context: Paul names the teacher who will not consent to the sound words of Jesus and the teaching that accords with godliness: conceit, controversy, and the fantasy that godliness is a means of gain. True gain is godliness with contentment; we brought nothing in and take nothing out. The love of money is a root of evils, and by that craving some have already wandered from the faith.
text: 1 Timothy 6:3–10 1 Timothy Paul names the teacher who will not consent to the sound words of Jesus and the teaching that accords with godliness: conceit, controversy, and the fantasy that godliness is a means of gain. True gain is godliness with contentment; we brought nothing in and take nothing out. The love of money is a root of evils, and by that craving some have already wandered from the faith. If anyone teaches a different doctrine and does not agree with the sound words of our Lord Jesus Christ and the teaching that accords with godliness, 1 Timothy 6:3 he is puffed up with conceit and understands nothing. He has an unhealthy craving for controversy and for quarrels about words, which produce envy, dissension, slander, evil suspicions, 1 Timothy 6:4 and constant friction among people who are depraved in mind and deprived of the truth, imagining that godliness is a means of gain. 1 Timothy 6:5 But godliness with contentment is great gain, 1 Timothy 6:6 for we brought nothing into the world, and we cannot take anything out of the world. 1 Timothy 6:7 But if we have food and clothing, with these we will be content. 1 Timothy 6:8 But those who desire to be rich fall into temptation, into a snare, into many senseless and harmful desires that plunge people into ruin and destruction. 1 Timothy 6:9 For the love of money is a root of all kinds of evils. It is through this craving that some have wandered away from the faith and pierced themselves with many pangs. 1 Timothy 6:10

title: 2 John 1:1–6
context: The elder writes to the elect lady and her children: love in the truth that abides forever; grace, mercy, and peace from the Father and the Father’s Son; joy that some of her children walk in the truth; then the old commandment, that we love one another—and this is love, that we walk according to his commandments.
text: 2 John 1:1–6 2 John The elder writes to the elect lady and her children: love in the truth that abides forever; grace, mercy, and peace from the Father and the Father’s Son; joy that some of her children walk in the truth; then the old commandment, that we love one another—and this is love, that we walk according to his commandments. The elder to the elect lady and her children, whom I love in truth, and not only I, but also all who know the truth, 2 John 1:1 because of the truth that abides in us and will be with us forever: 2 John 1:2 Grace, mercy, and peace will be with us, from God the Father and from Jesus Christ the Father’s Son, in truth and love. 2 John 1:3 I rejoiced greatly to find some of your children walking in the truth, just as we were commanded by the Father. 2 John 1:4 And now I ask you, dear lady—not as though I were writing you a new commandment, but the one we have had from the beginning—that we love one another. 2 John 1:5 And this is love, that we walk according to his commandments; this is the commandment, just as you have heard from the beginning, so that you should walk in it. 2 John 1:6

title: 2 John 1:7–13
context: The elder warns that many deceivers have gone out who do not confess the coming of Jesus Christ in the flesh—the deceiver and the antichrist. Watch, so as not to lose what was worked for; whoever goes on ahead and does not abide in the teaching of Christ does not have God. Do not receive such a one into the house or greet him, or you take part in his wicked works. Then paper yields to the hope of face-to-face speech, and the elect sister’s children greet her.
text: 2 John 1:7–13 2 John The elder warns that many deceivers have gone out who do not confess the coming of Jesus Christ in the flesh—the deceiver and the antichrist. Watch, so as not to lose what was worked for; whoever goes on ahead and does not abide in the teaching of Christ does not have God. Do not receive such a one into the house or greet him, or you take part in his wicked works. Then paper yields to the hope of face-to-face speech, and the elect sister’s children greet her. For many deceivers have gone out into the world, those who do not confess the coming of Jesus Christ in the flesh. Such a one is the deceiver and the antichrist. 2 John 1:7 Watch yourselves, so that you may not lose what we have worked for, but may win a full reward. 2 John 1:8 Everyone who goes on ahead and does not abide in the teaching of Christ, does not have God. Whoever abides in the teaching has both the Father and the Son. 2 John 1:9 If anyone comes to you and does not bring this teaching, do not receive him into your house or give him any greeting, 2 John 1:10 for whoever greets him takes part in his wicked works. 2 John 1:11 Though I have much to write to you, I would rather not use paper and ink. Instead I hope to come to you and talk face to face, so that our joy may be complete. 2 John 1:12 The children of your elect sister greet you. 2 John 1:13

title: 2 Timothy 1:1–7
context: Paul greets Timothy as his beloved child, an apostle by the will of God according to the promise of the life that is in Christ Jesus. He thanks God as he prays night and day, longs to see Timothy, recalls the sincere faith of Lois and Eunice now dwelling in him, and urges him to fan into flame the gift given through the laying on of hands—for God gave a spirit not of fear but of power, love, and self-control.
text: 2 Timothy 1:1–7 2 Timothy Paul greets Timothy as his beloved child, an apostle by the will of God according to the promise of the life that is in Christ Jesus. He thanks God as he prays night and day, longs to see Timothy, recalls the sincere faith of Lois and Eunice now dwelling in him, and urges him to fan into flame the gift given through the laying on of hands—for God gave a spirit not of fear but of power, love, and self-control. Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God according to the promise of the life that is in Christ Jesus, 2 Timothy 1:1 To Timothy, my beloved child: Grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord. 2 Timothy 1:2 I thank God whom I serve, as did my ancestors, with a clear conscience, as I remember you constantly in my prayers night and day. 2 Timothy 1:3 As I remember your tears, I long to see you, that I may be filled with joy. 2 Timothy 1:4 I am reminded of your sincere faith, a faith that dwelt first in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice and now, I am sure, dwells in you as well. 2 Timothy 1:5 For this reason I remind you to fan into flame the gift of God, which is in you through the laying on of my hands, 2 Timothy 1:6 for God gave us a spirit not of fear but of power and love and self-control. 2 Timothy 1:7

title: 2 Timothy 1:15–18
context: Paul names a hard fact: all who are in Asia turned away from him, Phygelus and Hermogenes among them. Against that desertion he asks mercy for the household of Onesiphorus, who often refreshed him, was not ashamed of his chains, searched him out in Rome, and had served well at Ephesus—that he may find mercy from the Lord on that day.
text: 2 Timothy 1:15–18 2 Timothy Paul names a hard fact: all who are in Asia turned away from him, Phygelus and Hermogenes among them. Against that desertion he asks mercy for the household of Onesiphorus, who often refreshed him, was not ashamed of his chains, searched him out in Rome, and had served well at Ephesus—that he may find mercy from the Lord on that day. You are aware that all who are in Asia turned away from me, among whom are Phygelus and Hermogenes. 2 Timothy 1:15 May the Lord grant mercy to the household of Onesiphorus, for he often refreshed me and was not ashamed of my chains, 2 Timothy 1:16 but when he arrived in Rome he searched for me earnestly and found me— 2 Timothy 1:17 may the Lord grant him to find mercy from the Lord on that day!—and you well know all the service he rendered at Ephesus. 2 Timothy 1:18

title: 2 Timothy 1:8–14
context: Paul charges Timothy not to be ashamed of the Lord’s testimony or of the apostle in chains, but to share gospel-suffering by God’s power. That power belongs to the God who saved and called them by his own purpose and grace, given in Christ Jesus before the ages began and now manifested in the Savior who abolished death; Paul is not ashamed, and Timothy must follow the pattern of sound words and guard the good deposit by the Spirit.
text: 2 Timothy 1:8–14 2 Timothy Paul charges Timothy not to be ashamed of the Lord’s testimony or of the apostle in chains, but to share gospel-suffering by God’s power. That power belongs to the God who saved and called them by his own purpose and grace, given in Christ Jesus before the ages began and now manifested in the Savior who abolished death; Paul is not ashamed, and Timothy must follow the pattern of sound words and guard the good deposit by the Spirit. Therefore do not be ashamed of the testimony about our Lord, nor of me his prisoner, but share in suffering for the gospel by the power of God, 2 Timothy 1:8 who saved us and called us to a holy calling, not because of our works but because of his own purpose and grace, which he gave us in Christ Jesus before the ages began, 2 Timothy 1:9 and which now has been manifested through the appearing of our Savior Christ Jesus, who abolished death and brought life and immortality to light through the gospel, 2 Timothy 1:10 for which I was appointed a preacher and apostle and teacher, 2 Timothy 1:11 which is why I suffer as I do. But I am not ashamed, for I know whom I have believed, and I am convinced that he is able to guard until that day what has been entrusted to me. 2 Timothy 1:12 Follow the pattern of the sound words that you have heard from me, in the faith and love that are in Christ Jesus. 2 Timothy 1:13 By the Holy Spirit who dwells within us, guard the good deposit entrusted to you. 2 Timothy 1:14

title: 2 Timothy 2:1–7
context: Paul charges Timothy, his child, to be strengthened by the grace that is in Christ Jesus and to entrust what he has heard to faithful men who can teach others. Soldier, athlete, and farmer pictures press undivided endurance, and the Lord himself will give understanding.
text: 2 Timothy 2:1–7 2 Timothy Paul charges Timothy, his child, to be strengthened by the grace that is in Christ Jesus and to entrust what he has heard to faithful men who can teach others. Soldier, athlete, and farmer pictures press undivided endurance, and the Lord himself will give understanding. You then, my child, be strengthened by the grace that is in Christ Jesus, 2 Timothy 2:1 and what you have heard from me in the presence of many witnesses entrust to faithful men, who will be able to teach others also. 2 Timothy 2:2 Share in suffering as a good soldier of Christ Jesus. 2 Timothy 2:3 No soldier gets entangled in civilian pursuits, since his aim is to please the one who enlisted him. 2 Timothy 2:4 An athlete is not crowned unless he competes according to the rules. 2 Timothy 2:5 It is the hard-working farmer who ought to have the first share of the crops. 2 Timothy 2:6 Think over what I say, for the Lord will give you understanding in everything. 2 Timothy 2:7

title: 2 Timothy 2:14–19
context: Timothy must remind the church not to quarrel about words, but to present himself to God as an approved worker, rightly handling the word of truth. Irreverent babble spreads like gangrene—Hymenaeus and Philetus have already upset some—yet God’s firm foundation stands with its double seal.
text: 2 Timothy 2:14–19 2 Timothy Timothy must remind the church not to quarrel about words, but to present himself to God as an approved worker, rightly handling the word of truth. Irreverent babble spreads like gangrene—Hymenaeus and Philetus have already upset some—yet God’s firm foundation stands with its double seal. Remind them of these things, and charge them before God not to quarrel about words, which does no good, but only ruins the hearers. 2 Timothy 2:14 Do your best to present yourself to God as one approved, a worker who has no need to be ashamed, rightly handling the word of truth. 2 Timothy 2:15 But avoid irreverent babble, for it will lead people into more and more ungodliness, 2 Timothy 2:16 and their talk will spread like gangrene. Among them are Hymenaeus and Philetus, 2 Timothy 2:17 who have swerved from the truth, saying that the resurrection has already happened. They are upsetting the faith of some. 2 Timothy 2:18 But God’s firm foundation stands, bearing this seal: “The Lord knows those who are his,” and, “Let everyone who names the name of the Lord depart from iniquity.” 2 Timothy 2:19

title: 2 Timothy 2:20–26
context: In a great house some vessels are for honor and some for dishonor; anyone who cleanses himself from what is dishonorable is useful to the Master. The Lord’s servant flees youthful passions, refuses foolish controversies, and corrects opponents with gentleness, hoping God may grant repentance and escape from the devil’s snare.
text: 2 Timothy 2:20–26 2 Timothy In a great house some vessels are for honor and some for dishonor; anyone who cleanses himself from what is dishonorable is useful to the Master. The Lord’s servant flees youthful passions, refuses foolish controversies, and corrects opponents with gentleness, hoping God may grant repentance and escape from the devil’s snare. Now in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and silver but also of wood and clay, some for honorable use, some for dishonorable. 2 Timothy 2:20 Therefore, if anyone cleanses himself from what is dishonorable, he will be a vessel for honorable use, set apart as holy, useful to the master of the house, ready for every good work. 2 Timothy 2:21 So flee youthful passions and pursue righteousness, faith, love, and peace, along with those who call on the Lord from a pure heart. 2 Timothy 2:22 Have nothing to do with foolish, ignorant controversies; you know that they breed quarrels. 2 Timothy 2:23 And the Lord’s servant must not be quarrelsome but kind to everyone, able to teach, patiently enduring evil, 2 Timothy 2:24 correcting his opponents with gentleness. God may perhaps grant them repentance leading to a knowledge of the truth, 2 Timothy 2:25 and they may come to their senses and escape from the snare of the devil, after being captured by him to do his will. 2 Timothy 2:26

title: 2 Timothy 2:8–13
context: Remember Jesus Christ, risen from the dead, the offspring of David: Paul is bound, but the word of God is not. He endures everything for the sake of the elect, that they may obtain salvation, and seals the charge with a trustworthy saying about dying, enduring, denying, and the Lord’s faithfulness.
text: 2 Timothy 2:8–13 2 Timothy Remember Jesus Christ, risen from the dead, the offspring of David: Paul is bound, but the word of God is not. He endures everything for the sake of the elect, that they may obtain salvation, and seals the charge with a trustworthy saying about dying, enduring, denying, and the Lord’s faithfulness. Remember Jesus Christ, risen from the dead, the offspring of David, as preached in my gospel, 2 Timothy 2:8 for which I am suffering, bound with chains as a criminal. But the word of God is not bound! 2 Timothy 2:9 Therefore I endure everything for the sake of the elect, that they also may obtain the salvation that is in Christ Jesus with eternal glory. 2 Timothy 2:10 The saying is trustworthy, for: If we have died with him, we will also live with him; 2 Timothy 2:11 if we endure, we will also reign with him; if we deny him, he also will deny us; 2 Timothy 2:12 if we are faithless, he remains faithful— for he cannot deny himself. 2 Timothy 2:13

title: 2 Timothy 3:1–9
context: Paul warns Timothy that last-days difficulty will rise inside the church: people will love self and pleasure more than God, keeping a form of godliness while denying its power. Some will capture the unstable, always learning yet never arriving at the truth—opposing it as Jannes and Jambres opposed Moses—yet their folly will not stay hidden.
text: 2 Timothy 3:1–9 2 Timothy Paul warns Timothy that last-days difficulty will rise inside the church: people will love self and pleasure more than God, keeping a form of godliness while denying its power. Some will capture the unstable, always learning yet never arriving at the truth—opposing it as Jannes and Jambres opposed Moses—yet their folly will not stay hidden. But understand this, that in the last days there will come times of difficulty. 2 Timothy 3:1 For people will be lovers of self, lovers of money, proud, arrogant, abusive, disobedient to their parents, ungrateful, unholy, 2 Timothy 3:2 heartless, unappeasable, slanderous, without self-control, brutal, not loving good, 2 Timothy 3:3 treacherous, reckless, swollen with conceit, lovers of pleasure rather than lovers of God, 2 Timothy 3:4 having the appearance of godliness, but denying its power. Avoid such people. 2 Timothy 3:5 For among them are those who creep into households and capture weak women, burdened with sins and led astray by various passions, 2 Timothy 3:6 always learning and never able to arrive at a knowledge of the truth. 2 Timothy 3:7 Just as Jannes and Jambres opposed Moses, so these men also oppose the truth, men corrupted in mind and disqualified regarding the faith. 2 Timothy 3:8 But they will not get very far, for their folly will be plain to all, as was that of those two men. 2 Timothy 3:9

title: 2 Timothy 3:10–17
context: Timothy is set over against the impostors: he has followed Paul’s teaching, conduct, faith, love, and sufferings, and the Lord rescued Paul from them all. All who desire a godly life in Christ will be persecuted, while evil people go from bad to worse. Timothy must continue in what he learned; the sacred writings are able to make him wise for salvation through faith in Christ Jesus, and all Scripture is God-breathed—profitable so that the man of God may be complete.
text: 2 Timothy 3:10–17 2 Timothy Timothy is set over against the impostors: he has followed Paul’s teaching, conduct, faith, love, and sufferings, and the Lord rescued Paul from them all. All who desire a godly life in Christ will be persecuted, while evil people go from bad to worse. Timothy must continue in what he learned; the sacred writings are able to make him wise for salvation through faith in Christ Jesus, and all Scripture is God-breathed—profitable so that the man of God may be complete. You, however, have followed my teaching, my conduct, my aim in life, my faith, my patience, my love, my steadfastness, 2 Timothy 3:10 my persecutions and sufferings that happened to me at Antioch, at Iconium, and at Lystra—which persecutions I endured; yet from them all the Lord rescued me. 2 Timothy 3:11 Indeed, all who desire to live a godly life in Christ Jesus will be persecuted, 2 Timothy 3:12 while evil people and impostors will go on from bad to worse, deceiving and being deceived. 2 Timothy 3:13 But as for you, continue in what you have learned and have firmly believed, knowing from whom you learned it 2 Timothy 3:14 and how from childhood you have been acquainted with the sacred writings, which are able to make you wise for salvation through faith in Christ Jesus. 2 Timothy 3:15 All Scripture is breathed out by God and profitable for teaching, for reproof, for correction, and for training in righteousness, 2 Timothy 3:16 that the man of God may be complete, equipped for every good work. 2 Timothy 3:17

title: 2 Timothy 4:1–8
context: Paul charges Timothy before God and Christ Jesus, the coming Judge: preach the word in season and out, with patience and teaching, because people will not endure sound doctrine. Timothy must stay sober-minded, endure suffering, do an evangelist’s work, and fulfill his ministry. Paul is already poured out; he has fought the good fight, finished the race, and kept the faith—and a crown of righteousness awaits him and all who have loved the Lord’s appearing.
text: 2 Timothy 4:1–8 2 Timothy Paul charges Timothy before God and Christ Jesus, the coming Judge: preach the word in season and out, with patience and teaching, because people will not endure sound doctrine. Timothy must stay sober-minded, endure suffering, do an evangelist’s work, and fulfill his ministry. Paul is already poured out; he has fought the good fight, finished the race, and kept the faith—and a crown of righteousness awaits him and all who have loved the Lord’s appearing. I charge you in the presence of God and of Christ Jesus, who is to judge the living and the dead, and by his appearing and his kingdom: 2 Timothy 4:1 preach the word; be ready in season and out of season; reprove, rebuke, and exhort, with complete patience and teaching. 2 Timothy 4:2 For the time is coming when people will not endure sound teaching, but having itching ears they will accumulate for themselves teachers to suit their own passions, 2 Timothy 4:3 and will turn away from listening to the truth and wander off into myths. 2 Timothy 4:4 But as for you, always be sober-minded, endure suffering, do the work of an evangelist, fulfill your ministry. 2 Timothy 4:5 For I am already being poured out as a drink offering, and the time of my departure has come. 2 Timothy 4:6 I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith. 2 Timothy 4:7 Henceforth there is laid up for me the crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous judge, will award to me on that day, and not only to me but also to all who have loved his appearing. 2 Timothy 4:8

title: 2 Timothy 4:16–22
context: At Paul’s first defense no one stood by him; all deserted, and he asks that it not be charged against them. The Lord stood by him and strengthened him so the message was fully proclaimed to the Gentiles, and he was rescued from the lion’s mouth. He trusts the Lord to rescue him from every evil deed and bring him safely into the heavenly kingdom. Greetings follow—Prisca, Aquila, Onesiphorus’s household—and a last plea to come before winter, with grace.
text: 2 Timothy 4:16–22 2 Timothy At Paul’s first defense no one stood by him; all deserted, and he asks that it not be charged against them. The Lord stood by him and strengthened him so the message was fully proclaimed to the Gentiles, and he was rescued from the lion’s mouth. He trusts the Lord to rescue him from every evil deed and bring him safely into the heavenly kingdom. Greetings follow—Prisca, Aquila, Onesiphorus’s household—and a last plea to come before winter, with grace. At my first defense no one came to stand by me, but all deserted me. May it not be charged against them! 2 Timothy 4:16 But the Lord stood by me and strengthened me, so that through me the message might be fully proclaimed and all the Gentiles might hear it. So I was rescued from the lion's mouth. 2 Timothy 4:17 The Lord will rescue me from every evil deed and bring me safely into his heavenly kingdom. To him be the glory forever and ever. Amen. 2 Timothy 4:18 Greet Prisca and Aquila, and the household of Onesiphorus. 2 Timothy 4:19 Erastus remained at Corinth, and I left Trophimus, who was ill, at Miletus. 2 Timothy 4:20 Do your best to come before winter. Eubulus sends greetings to you, as do Pudens and Linus and Claudia and all the brothers. 2 Timothy 4:21 The Lord be with your spirit. Grace be with you. 2 Timothy 4:22

title: 2 Timothy 4:9–15
context: Paul turns to personal need: come soon. Demas, in love with this present world, has deserted him; Crescens and Titus are away; Luke alone remains. Mark, once a departure story himself, is now useful—bring him. Tychicus has been sent to Ephesus. Bring the cloak, the books, and above all the parchments. Alexander the coppersmith did great harm and opposed the message; the Lord will repay him, and Timothy must beware.
text: 2 Timothy 4:9–15 2 Timothy Paul turns to personal need: come soon. Demas, in love with this present world, has deserted him; Crescens and Titus are away; Luke alone remains. Mark, once a departure story himself, is now useful—bring him. Tychicus has been sent to Ephesus. Bring the cloak, the books, and above all the parchments. Alexander the coppersmith did great harm and opposed the message; the Lord will repay him, and Timothy must beware. Do your best to come to me soon. 2 Timothy 4:9 For Demas, in love with this present world, has deserted me and gone to Thessalonica. Crescens has gone to Galatia, Titus to Dalmatia. 2 Timothy 4:10 Luke alone is with me. Get Mark and bring him with you, for he is very useful to me for ministry. 2 Timothy 4:11 Tychicus I have sent to Ephesus. 2 Timothy 4:12 When you come, bring the cloak that I left with Carpus at Troas, also the books, and above all the parchments. 2 Timothy 4:13 Alexander the coppersmith did me great harm; the Lord will repay him according to his deeds. 2 Timothy 4:14 Beware of him yourself, for he strongly opposed our message. 2 Timothy 4:15

title: 3 John 1:1–8
context: The elder writes to the beloved Gaius, whom he loves in truth: prayer that body and affairs would match a prospering soul; joy that the brothers testified to Gaius’s walking in the truth; then praise for faithful work toward traveling brothers—strangers who have gone out for the Name, taking nothing from the Gentiles—so that those who send them are fellow workers for the truth.
text: 3 John 1:1–8 3 John The elder writes to the beloved Gaius, whom he loves in truth: prayer that body and affairs would match a prospering soul; joy that the brothers testified to Gaius’s walking in the truth; then praise for faithful work toward traveling brothers—strangers who have gone out for the Name, taking nothing from the Gentiles—so that those who send them are fellow workers for the truth. The elder to the beloved Gaius, whom I love in truth. 3 John 1:1 Beloved, I pray that all may go well with you and that you may be in good health, as it goes well with your soul. 3 John 1:2 For I rejoiced greatly when the brothers came and testified to your truth, as indeed you are walking in the truth. 3 John 1:3 I have no greater joy than to hear that my children are walking in the truth. 3 John 1:4 Beloved, it is a faithful thing you do in all your efforts for these brothers, strangers as they are, 3 John 1:5 who testified to your love before the church. You will do well to send them on their journey in a manner worthy of God. 3 John 1:6 For they have gone out for the sake of the name, accepting nothing from the Gentiles. 3 John 1:7 Therefore we ought to support people like these, that we may be fellow workers for the truth. 3 John 1:8

title: 3 John 1:9–15
context: The elder had written to the church, but Diotrephes, who loves to be first, will not acknowledge apostolic authority: wicked nonsense, refusal to welcome the brothers, stopping those who would, putting them out. Gaius is told not to imitate evil but good—whoever does good is from God; whoever does evil has not seen God. Demetrius has a good testimony from everyone and from the truth. Then pen and ink yield to the hope of face-to-face speech, peace, and friends greeted by name.
text: 3 John 1:9–15 3 John The elder had written to the church, but Diotrephes, who loves to be first, will not acknowledge apostolic authority: wicked nonsense, refusal to welcome the brothers, stopping those who would, putting them out. Gaius is told not to imitate evil but good—whoever does good is from God; whoever does evil has not seen God. Demetrius has a good testimony from everyone and from the truth. Then pen and ink yield to the hope of face-to-face speech, peace, and friends greeted by name. I have written something to the church, but Diotrephes, who likes to put himself first, does not acknowledge our authority. 3 John 1:9 So if I come, I will bring up what he is doing, talking wicked nonsense against us. And not content with that, he refuses to welcome the brothers, and also stops those who want to and puts them out of the church. 3 John 1:10 Beloved, do not imitate evil but imitate good. Whoever does good is from God; whoever does evil has not seen God. 3 John 1:11 Demetrius has received a good testimony from everyone, and from the truth itself. We also add our testimony, and you know that our testimony is true. 3 John 1:12 I had much to write to you, but I would rather not write with pen and ink. 3 John 1:13 I hope to see you soon, and we will talk face to face. 3 John 1:14 Peace be to you. The friends greet you. Greet the friends, each by name. 3 John 1:15

title: Colossians 1:1–14
context: Paul greets the Colossian saints with Timothy, then thanks God for their faith, love, and hope rooted in the gospel that is bearing fruit worldwide. He keeps praying that they would be filled with knowledge of God’s will, walk worthy of the Lord, and remember the Father’s rescue: delivered from darkness, transferred into the Son’s kingdom, and given redemption—the forgiveness of sins.
text: Colossians 1:1–14 Colossians Paul greets the Colossian saints with Timothy, then thanks God for their faith, love, and hope rooted in the gospel that is bearing fruit worldwide.
