I am he; I am the first, and I am the last. Isaiah 48:12 My hand laid the foundation of the earth, and my right hand spread out the heavens; when I call to them, they stand forth together. Isaiah 48:13 “Assemble, all of you, and listen! Who among them has declared these things? The LORD loves him; he shall perform his purpose on Babylon, and his arm shall be against the Chaldeans. Isaiah 48:14 I, even I, have spoken and called him; I have brought him, and he will prosper in his way. Isaiah 48:15 Draw near to me, hear this: from the beginning I have not spoken in secret, from the time it came to be I have been there.” And now the Lord GOD has sent me, and his Spirit. Isaiah 48:16 Thus says the LORD, your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel: “I am the LORD your God, who teaches you to profit, who leads you in the way you should go. Isaiah 48:17 Oh that you had paid attention to my commandments! Then your peace would have been like a river, and your righteousness like the waves of the sea; Isaiah 48:18 your offspring would have been like the sand, and your descendants like its grains; their name would never be cut off or destroyed from before me.” Isaiah 48:19 Go out from Babylon, flee from Chaldea, declare this with a shout of joy, proclaim it, send it out to the end of the earth; say, “The LORD has redeemed his servant Jacob!” Isaiah 48:20 They did not thirst when he led them through the deserts; he made water flow for them from the rock; he split the rock and the water gushed out. Isaiah 48:21 “There is no peace,” says the LORD, “for the wicked.” Isaiah 48:22

title: Isaiah 49:1–7
context: The Servant of the LORD addresses coastlands and peoples from afar: called from the womb, a mouth like a sword, named Israel in whom God will be glorified. Labor among Jacob seemed vain, yet the LORD makes him a light for the nations so that salvation reaches the end of the earth; the despised servant of rulers will see kings arise.
text: Isaiah 49:1–7 Isaiah The Servant of the LORD addresses coastlands and peoples from afar: called from the womb, a mouth like a sword, named Israel in whom God will be glorified. Labor among Jacob seemed vain, yet the LORD makes him a light for the nations so that salvation reaches the end of the earth; the despised servant of rulers will see kings arise. Listen to me, O coastlands, and give attention, you peoples from afar. The LORD called me from the womb, from the body of my mother he named my name. Isaiah 49:1 He made my mouth like a sharp sword; in the shadow of his hand he hid me; he made me a polished arrow; in his quiver he hid me away. Isaiah 49:2 And he said to me, “You are my servant, Israel, in whom I will be glorified.” Isaiah 49:3 But I said, “I have labored in vain; I have spent my strength for nothing and vanity; yet surely my right is with the LORD, and my recompense with my God.” Isaiah 49:4 And now the LORD says, he who formed me from the womb to be his servant, to bring Jacob back to him; and that Israel might be gathered to him—for I am honored in the eyes of the LORD, and my God has become my strength— Isaiah 49:5 he says: “It is too light a thing that you should be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob and to bring back the preserved of Israel; I will make you as a light for the nations, that my salvation may reach to the end of the earth.” Isaiah 49:6 Thus says the LORD, the Redeemer of Israel and his Holy One, to one deeply despised, abhorred by the nation, the servant of rulers: “Kings shall see and arise; princes, and they shall prostrate themselves; because of the LORD, who is faithful, the Holy One of Israel, who has chosen you.” Isaiah 49:7

title: Isaiah 49:14–26
context: Zion says the LORD has forsaken her; he answers that a woman may forget her nursing child, yet he will not forget, for he has engraved her on his palms. Children crowd the waste places; captives of the mighty are rescued; all flesh shall know that he is the LORD, Savior and Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob.
text: Isaiah 49:14–26 Isaiah Zion says the LORD has forsaken her; he answers that a woman may forget her nursing child, yet he will not forget, for he has engraved her on his palms. Children crowd the waste places; captives of the mighty are rescued; all flesh shall know that he is the LORD, Savior and Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob. But Zion said, “The LORD has forsaken me; my Lord has forgotten me.” Isaiah 49:14 “Can a woman forget her nursing child, that she should have no compassion on the son of her womb? Even these may forget, yet I will not forget you. Isaiah 49:15 Behold, I have engraved you on the palms of my hands; your walls are continually before me. Isaiah 49:16 Your builders make haste; your destroyers and those who laid you waste go out from you. Isaiah 49:17 Lift up your eyes around and see; they all gather, they come to you. As I live, declares the LORD, you shall put them all on as an ornament; you shall bind them on as a bride does. Isaiah 49:18 Surely your waste and your desolate places and your devastated land—surely now you will be too narrow for your inhabitants, and those who swallowed you up will be far away. Isaiah 49:19 The children of your bereavement will yet say in your ears: ‘The place is too narrow for me; make room for me to dwell in.’ Isaiah 49:20 Then you will say in your heart: ‘Who has borne me these? I was bereaved and barren, exiled and put away, but who has brought up these? Behold, I was left alone; from where have these come?’” Isaiah 49:21 Thus says the Lord GOD: “Behold, I will lift up my hand to the nations, and raise my signal to the peoples; and they shall bring your sons in their arms, and your daughters shall be carried on their shoulders. Isaiah 49:22 Kings shall be your foster fathers, and their queens your nursing mothers. With their faces to the ground they shall bow down to you, and lick the dust of your feet. Then you will know that I am the LORD; those who wait for me shall not be put to shame.” Isaiah 49:23 Can the prey be taken from the mighty, or the captives of a tyrant be rescued? Isaiah 49:24 For thus says the LORD: “Even the captives of the mighty shall be taken, and the prey of the tyrant be rescued, for I will contend with those who contend with you, and I will save your children. Isaiah 49:25 I will make your oppressors eat their own flesh, and they shall be drunk with their own blood as with wine. Then all flesh shall know that I am the LORD your Savior, and your Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob.” Isaiah 49:26

title: Isaiah 49:8–13
context: The LORD answers the Servant in a time of favor and a day of salvation, keeps him and gives him as a covenant to the people to establish the land. Prisoners are told to come out; they shall not hunger or thirst; mountains become a road; they come from afar; heavens and earth sing because the LORD has comforted his people and will have compassion on the afflicted.
text: Isaiah 49:8–13 Isaiah The LORD answers the Servant in a time of favor and a day of salvation, keeps him and gives him as a covenant to the people to establish the land. Prisoners are told to come out; they shall not hunger or thirst; mountains become a road; they come from afar; heavens and earth sing because the LORD has comforted his people and will have compassion on the afflicted. Thus says the LORD: “In a time of favor I have answered you; in a day of salvation I have helped you; I will keep you and give you as a covenant to the people, to establish the land, to apportion the desolate heritages, Isaiah 49:8 saying to the prisoners, ‘Come out,’ to those who are in darkness, ‘Appear.’ They shall feed along the ways; on all bare heights shall be their pasture; Isaiah 49:9 they shall not hunger or thirst, neither scorching wind nor sun shall strike them, for he who has pity on them will lead them, and by springs of water will guide them. Isaiah 49:10 And I will make all my mountains a road, and my highways shall be raised up. Isaiah 49:11 Behold, these shall come from afar, and behold, these from the north and from the west, and these from the land of Syene.” Isaiah 49:12 Sing for joy, O heavens, and exult, O earth; break forth, O mountains, into singing! For the LORD has comforted his people and will have compassion on his afflicted. Isaiah 49:13

title: Isaiah 5:1–7
context: Isaiah sings for his beloved a song of a vineyard on a fertile hill. The beloved digs, clears stones, plants choice vines, builds a tower, hews a vat, and looks for grapes. Wild grapes come. Jerusalem and Judah are told to judge. What more was there to do? The hedge will be removed, the wall broken, briers will grow, the clouds commanded not to rain. The vineyard is the house of Israel; Judah his pleasant planting. He looked for justice, and behold, bloodshed; for righteousness, an outcry.
text: Isaiah 5:1–7 Isaiah Isaiah sings for his beloved a song of a vineyard on a fertile hill. The beloved digs, clears stones, plants choice vines, builds a tower, hews a vat, and looks for grapes. Wild grapes come. Jerusalem and Judah are told to judge. What more was there to do? The hedge will be removed, the wall broken, briers will grow, the clouds commanded not to rain. The vineyard is the house of Israel; Judah his pleasant planting. He looked for justice, and behold, bloodshed; for righteousness, an outcry. Let me sing for my beloved my love song concerning his vineyard: My beloved had a vineyard on a very fertile hill. Isaiah 5:1 He dug it and cleared it of stones, and planted it with choice vines; he built a watchtower in the midst of it, and hewed out a wine vat in it; and he looked for it to yield grapes, but it yielded wild grapes. Isaiah 5:2 And now, O inhabitants of Jerusalem and men of Judah, judge, I pray you, between me and my vineyard. Isaiah 5:3 What more was there to do for my vineyard, that I have not done in it? When I looked for it to yield grapes, why did it yield wild grapes? Isaiah 5:4 And now I will tell you what I will do to my vineyard. I will remove its hedge, and it shall be devoured; I will break down its wall, and it shall be trampled down. Isaiah 5:5 I will make it a waste; it shall not be pruned or hoed, and briers and thorns shall grow up; I will also command the clouds that they rain no rain upon it. Isaiah 5:6 For the vineyard of the Lord of hosts is the house of Israel, and the men of Judah are his pleasant planting; and he looked for justice, but behold, bloodshed; for righteousness, but behold, an outcry! Isaiah 5:7

title: Isaiah 5:18–30
context: Woe to those who haul sin with cart ropes and dare the Holy One to hurry. Woe to those who swap good and evil, who are wise in their own eyes, heroes at drink, who acquit for a bribe. Fire eats stubble: they have rejected the law. His anger is kindled; the hand is stretched out still. He whistles for nations from the ends of the earth. They come swift, unsleeping, hoofs like flint, roaring like lions. On that day, darkness over the land.
text: Isaiah 5:18–30 Isaiah Woe to those who haul sin with cart ropes and dare the Holy One to hurry. Woe to those who swap good and evil, who are wise in their own eyes, heroes at drink, who acquit for a bribe. Fire eats stubble: they have rejected the law. His anger is kindled; the hand is stretched out still. He whistles for nations from the ends of the earth. They come swift, unsleeping, hoofs like flint, roaring like lions. On that day, darkness over the land. Woe to those who draw iniquity with cords of falsehood, who draw sin as with cart ropes, Isaiah 5:18 who say: “Let him be quick, let him speed his work that we may see it; let the counsel of the Holy One of Israel draw near, and let it come, that we may know it!” Isaiah 5:19 Woe to those who call evil good and good evil, who put darkness for light and light for darkness, who put bitter for sweet and sweet for bitter! Isaiah 5:20 Woe to those who are wise in their own eyes, and shrewd in their own sight! Isaiah 5:21 Woe to those who are heroes at drinking wine, and valiant men in mixing strong drink, Isaiah 5:22 who acquit the guilty for a bribe, and deprive the innocent of his right! Isaiah 5:23 Therefore, as the tongue of fire devours the stubble, and as dry grass sinks down in the flame, so their root will be as rottenness, and their blossom go up like dust; for they have rejected the law of the Lord of hosts, and have despised the word of the Holy One of Israel. Isaiah 5:24 Therefore the anger of the Lord was kindled against his people, and he stretched out his hand against them and struck them, and the mountains quaked; and their corpses were as refuse in the midst of the streets. For all this his anger has not turned away, and his hand is stretched out still. Isaiah 5:25 He will raise a signal for nations far away, and whistle for them from the ends of the earth; and behold, quickly, speedily they come! Isaiah 5:26 None is weary, none stumbles, none slumbers or sleeps, not a waistband is loose, not a sandal strap broken; Isaiah 5:27 their arrows are sharp, all their bows bent, their horses' hoofs seem like flint, and their wheels like the whirlwind. Isaiah 5:28 Their roaring is like a lion, like young lions they roar; they growl and seize their prey; they carry it off, and none can rescue. Isaiah 5:29 They will growl over it on that day, like the growling of the sea. And if one looks to the land, behold, darkness and distress; and the light is darkened by its clouds. Isaiah 5:30

title: Isaiah 5:8–17
context: After the vineyard’s wild grapes, woes fall on those who join house to house until they dwell alone, and on those who rise early for drink and feast without regarding the Lord’s work. Many houses will stand empty; ten acres yield a bath. Therefore the people go into exile for lack of knowledge; Sheol opens wide. Man is humbled; the Lord of hosts is exalted in justice. Then lambs graze, and nomads eat among the ruins of the rich.
text: Isaiah 5:8–17 Isaiah After the vineyard’s wild grapes, woes fall on those who join house to house until they dwell alone, and on those who rise early for drink and feast without regarding the Lord’s work. Many houses will stand empty; ten acres yield a bath. Therefore the people go into exile for lack of knowledge; Sheol opens wide. Man is humbled; the Lord of hosts is exalted in justice. Then lambs graze, and nomads eat among the ruins of the rich. Woe to those who join house to house, who add field to field, until there is no more room, and you are made to dwell alone in the midst of the land. Isaiah 5:8 The Lord of hosts has sworn in my hearing: “Surely many houses shall be desolate, large and beautiful houses, without inhabitant. Isaiah 5:9 For ten acres of vineyard shall yield but one bath, and a homer of seed shall yield but an ephah.” Isaiah 5:10 Woe to those who rise early in the morning, that they may run after strong drink, who tarry late into the evening as wine inflames them! Isaiah 5:11 They have lyre and harp, tambourine and flute and wine at their feasts, but they do not regard the deeds of the Lord, or see the work of his hands. Isaiah 5:12 Therefore my people go into exile for lack of knowledge; their honored men go hungry, and their multitude is parched with thirst. Isaiah 5:13 Therefore Sheol has enlarged its appetite and opened its mouth beyond measure, and the nobility of Jerusalem and her multitude will go down, her revelers and he who exults in her. Isaiah 5:14 Man is humbled, and each one is brought low, and the eyes of the haughty are brought low. Isaiah 5:15 But the Lord of hosts is exalted in justice, and the Holy God shows himself holy in righteousness. Isaiah 5:16 Then shall the lambs graze as in their pasture, and nomads shall eat among the ruins of the rich. Isaiah 5:17

title: Isaiah 50:1–11
context: The LORD asks Judah for a bill of divorce and names no bankrupt creditor: they were sold for iniquities, the mother sent away for transgressions. The Servant’s ear is opened; he is not rebellious, gives his back to those who strike, and is not put to shame; those who walk in darkness must trust the LORD, while torch-kindlers lie down in torment.
text: Isaiah 50:1–11 Isaiah The LORD asks Judah for a bill of divorce and names no bankrupt creditor: they were sold for iniquities, the mother sent away for transgressions. The Servant’s ear is opened; he is not rebellious, gives his back to those who strike, and is not put to shame; those who walk in darkness must trust the LORD, while torch-kindlers lie down in torment. Thus says the LORD: “Where is your mother’s certificate of divorce, with which I sent her away? Or which of my creditors is it to whom I have sold you? Behold, for your iniquities you were sold, and for your transgressions your mother was sent away.” Isaiah 50:1 Why, when I came, was there no man; why, when I called, was there no one to answer? Is my hand shortened, that it cannot redeem? Or have I no power to deliver? Behold, by my rebuke I dry up the sea, I make the rivers a desert; their fish stink for lack of water and die of thirst. Isaiah 50:2 I clothe the heavens with blackness and make sackcloth their covering. Isaiah 50:3 The Lord GOD has given me the tongue of those who are taught, that I may know how to sustain with a word him who is weary. Morning by morning he awakens; he awakens my ear to hear as those who are taught. Isaiah 50:4 The Lord GOD has opened my ear, and I was not rebellious; I turned not backward. Isaiah 50:5 I gave my back to those who strike, and my cheeks to those who pull out the beard; I hid not my face from disgrace and spitting. Isaiah 50:6 But the Lord GOD helps me; therefore I have not been disgraced; therefore I have set my face like a flint, and I know that I shall not be put to shame. Isaiah 50:7 He who vindicates me is near. Who will contend with me? Let us stand up together. Who is my adversary? Let him come near to me. Isaiah 50:8 Behold, the Lord GOD helps me; who will declare me guilty? Behold, all of them will wear out like a garment; the moth will eat them up. Isaiah 50:9 Who among you fears the LORD and obeys the voice of his servant? Let him who walks in darkness and has no light trust in the name of the LORD and rely on his God. Isaiah 50:10 Behold, all you who kindle a fire, who equip yourselves with burning torches! Walk by the light of your fire, and by the torches that you have kindled! This you have from my hand: you shall lie down in torment. Isaiah 50:11

title: Isaiah 51:1–8
context: Those who pursue righteousness are told to look to Abraham and Sarah—the rock and the quarry—because the LORD who called one man can still comfort Zion’s wastes like Eden. A law goes out as light to the peoples; his righteousness and salvation outlast heavens and earth, so the people in whose heart is his law need not fear the reproach of men.
text: Isaiah 51:1–8 Isaiah Those who pursue righteousness are told to look to Abraham and Sarah—the rock and the quarry—because the LORD who called one man can still comfort Zion’s wastes like Eden. A law goes out as light to the peoples; his righteousness and salvation outlast heavens and earth, so the people in whose heart is his law need not fear the reproach of men. Listen to me, you who pursue righteousness, you who seek the LORD: look to the rock from which you were hewn, and to the quarry from which you were dug. Isaiah 51:1 Look to Abraham your father and to Sarah who bore you; for he was but one when I called him, that I might bless him and multiply him. Isaiah 51:2 For the LORD comforts Zion; he comforts all her waste places and makes her wilderness like Eden, her desert like the garden of the LORD; joy and gladness will be found in her, thanksgiving and the voice of song. Isaiah 51:3 Give attention to me, my people, and give ear to me, my nation; for a law will go out from me, and I will set my justice for a light to the peoples. Isaiah 51:4 My righteousness draws near, my salvation has gone out, and my arms will judge the peoples; the coastlands hope for me, and for my arm they wait. Isaiah 51:5 Lift up your eyes to the heavens, and look at the earth beneath; for the heavens vanish like smoke, the earth will wear out like a garment, and they who dwell in it will die in like manner; but my salvation will be forever, and my righteousness will never be dismayed. Isaiah 51:6 Listen to me, you who know righteousness, the people in whose heart is my law; fear not the reproach of man, nor be dismayed at their revilings. Isaiah 51:7 For the moth will eat them up like a garment, and the worm will eat them like wool; but my righteousness will be forever, and my salvation to all generations. Isaiah 51:8

title: Isaiah 51:17–23
context: Jerusalem is told to wake herself and stand after drinking from the LORD's hand the cup of his wrath to the dregs—the historic staggering of Judah. Then the gospel turn: that cup is taken from her hand and put into the hand of her tormentors, who had made her back like the street.
text: Isaiah 51:17–23 Isaiah Jerusalem is told to wake herself and stand after drinking from the LORD's hand the cup of his wrath to the dregs—the historic staggering of Judah. Then the gospel turn: that cup is taken from her hand and put into the hand of her tormentors, who had made her back like the street. Wake yourself, wake yourself, stand up, O Jerusalem, you who have drunk from the hand of the LORD the cup of his wrath, who have drunk to the dregs the bowl, the cup of staggering. Isaiah 51:17 There is none to guide her among all the sons she has borne; there is none to take her by the hand among all the sons she has brought up. Isaiah 51:18 These two things have happened to you—who will console you?—devastation and destruction, famine and sword; who will comfort you? Isaiah 51:19 Your sons have fainted; they lie at the head of every street like an antelope in a net; they are full of the wrath of the LORD, the rebuke of your God. Isaiah 51:20 Therefore hear this, you who are afflicted, who are drunk, but not with wine: Isaiah 51:21 Thus says your Lord, the LORD, your God who pleads the cause of his people: "Behold, I have taken from your hand the cup of staggering; the bowl of my wrath you shall drink no more; Isaiah 51:22 and I will put it into the hand of your tormentors, who have said to you, 'Bow down, that we may pass over'; and you have made your back like the ground and like the street for them to pass over." Isaiah 51:23

title: Isaiah 51:9–16
context: The godly cry Awake, awake to the arm that cut Rahab and pierced the dragon at the sea, and the LORD answers: I, I am he who comforts you; do not fear the dying oppressor. He who is bowed down shall be set free; the LORD who stirs the sea puts his words in the mouth and covers with his hand, and says to Zion, You are my people.
text: Isaiah 51:9–16 Isaiah The godly cry Awake, awake to the arm that cut Rahab and pierced the dragon at the sea, and the LORD answers: I, I am he who comforts you; do not fear the dying oppressor. He who is bowed down shall be set free; the LORD who stirs the sea puts his words in the mouth and covers with his hand, and says to Zion, You are my people. Awake, awake, put on strength, O arm of the LORD; awake, as in days of old, the generations of long ago. Was it not you who cut Rahab in pieces, who pierced the dragon? Isaiah 51:9 Was it not you who dried up the sea, the waters of the great deep, who made the depths of the sea a way for the redeemed to pass over? Isaiah 51:10 And the ransomed of the LORD shall return and come to Zion with singing; everlasting joy shall be upon their heads; they shall obtain gladness and joy, and sorrow and sighing shall flee away. Isaiah 51:11 I, I am he who comforts you; who are you that you are afraid of man who dies, of the son of man who is made like grass, Isaiah 51:12 and have forgotten the LORD, your Maker, who stretched out the heavens and laid the foundations of the earth, and you fear continually all the day because of the wrath of the oppressor, when he sets himself to destroy? And where is the wrath of the oppressor? Isaiah 51:13 He who is bowed down shall speedily be released; he shall not die and go down to the pit, neither shall his bread be lacking. Isaiah 51:14 I am the LORD your God, who stirs up the sea so that its waves roar—the LORD of hosts is his name. Isaiah 51:15 And I have put my words in your mouth and covered you in the shadow of my hand, establishing the heavens and laying the foundations of the earth, and saying to Zion, 'You are my people.' Isaiah 51:16

title: Isaiah 52:1–12
context: Zion is told to awake and put on her strength and beautiful garments: historic Jerusalem, shake yourself from the dust, O captive daughter. Then the gospel turn: how beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of him who brings good news; the LORD has redeemed Jerusalem; depart, go out from there—not in haste, for the LORD will go before you.
text: Isaiah 52:1–12 Isaiah Zion is told to awake and put on her strength and beautiful garments: historic Jerusalem, shake yourself from the dust, O captive daughter. Then the gospel turn: how beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of him who brings good news; the LORD has redeemed Jerusalem; depart, go out from there—not in haste, for the LORD will go before you. Awake, awake, put on your strength, O Zion; put on your beautiful garments, O Jerusalem, the holy city; for there shall no more come into you the uncircumcised and the unclean. Isaiah 52:1 Shake yourself from the dust and arise; be seated, O Jerusalem; loose the bonds from your neck, O captive daughter of Zion. Isaiah 52:2 For thus says the LORD: "You were sold for nothing, and you shall be redeemed without money." Isaiah 52:3 For thus says the Lord GOD: "My people went down at the first into Egypt to sojourn there, and the Assyrian oppressed them for nothing. Isaiah 52:4 Now therefore what have I here," declares the LORD, "seeing that my people are taken away for nothing? Their rulers wail," declares the LORD, "and continually all the day my name is despised. Isaiah 52:5 Therefore my people shall know my name. Therefore in that day they shall know that it is I who speak; here I am." Isaiah 52:6 How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of him who brings good news, who publishes peace, who brings good news of happiness, who publishes salvation, who says to Zion, "Your God reigns." Isaiah 52:7 The voice of your watchmen—they lift up their voice; together they sing for joy; for eye to eye they see the return of the LORD to Zion. Isaiah 52:8 Break forth together into singing, you waste places of Jerusalem, for the LORD has comforted his people; he has redeemed Jerusalem. Isaiah 52:9 The LORD has bared his holy arm before the eyes of all the nations, and all the ends of the earth shall see the salvation of our God. Isaiah 52:10 Depart, depart, go out from there; touch no unclean thing; go out from the midst of her; purify yourselves, you who bear the vessels of the LORD. Isaiah 52:11 For you shall not go out in haste, and you shall not go in flight, for the LORD will go before you, and the God of Israel will be your rear guard. Isaiah 52:12

title: Isaiah 52:13–15
context: After Zion awakes and goes out of Babylon not in haste, a new prophecy opens: Behold, my servant shall act wisely; he shall be high and lifted up. Many were astonished at a visage marred beyond human semblance; so shall he sprinkle many nations, and kings shut their mouths because of him. Historic Servant first, then the gospel of that same Christ.
text: Isaiah 52:13–15 Isaiah After Zion awakes and goes out of Babylon not in haste, a new prophecy opens: Behold, my servant shall act wisely; he shall be high and lifted up. Many were astonished at a visage marred beyond human semblance; so shall he sprinkle many nations, and kings shut their mouths because of him. Historic Servant first, then the gospel of that same Christ. Behold, my servant shall act wisely; he shall be high and lifted up, and shall be exalted. Isaiah 52:13 As many were astonished at you—his appearance was so marred, beyond human semblance, and his form beyond that of the children of mankind— Isaiah 52:14 so shall he sprinkle many nations. Kings shall shut their mouths because of him, for that which has not been told them they see, and that which they have not heard they understand. Isaiah 52:15

title: Isaiah 53:1–12
context: The fourth servant song continues from 52:13: who has believed our report, and to whom is the arm of the LORD revealed? The Servant grows up like a root from dry ground, despised, a man of sorrows; yet he bears our griefs, is pierced for our transgressions, and the LORD lays on him the iniquity of us all. Like a lamb led to the slaughter he opens not his mouth; cut off from the land of the living, he makes his soul an offering for guilt, justifies many, and makes intercession for the transgressors. Historic Servant, then the gospel of that same Christ—substitution heard by both camps.
text: Isaiah 53:1–12 Isaiah The fourth servant song continues from 52:13: who has believed our report, and to whom is the arm of the LORD revealed? The Servant grows up like a root from dry ground, despised, a man of sorrows; yet he bears our griefs, is pierced for our transgressions, and the LORD lays on him the iniquity of us all. Like a lamb led to the slaughter he opens not his mouth; cut off from the land of the living, he makes his soul an offering for guilt, justifies many, and makes intercession for the transgressors. Historic Servant, then the gospel of that same Christ—substitution heard by both camps. Who has believed what he has heard from us? And to whom has the arm of the LORD been revealed? Isaiah 53:1 For he grew up before him like a young plant, and like a root out of dry ground; he had no form or majesty that we should look at him, and no beauty that we should desire him. Isaiah 53:2 He was despised and rejected by men, a man of sorrows and acquainted with grief; and as one from whom men hide their faces he was despised, and we esteemed him not. Isaiah 53:3 Surely he has borne our griefs and carried our sorrows; yet we esteemed him stricken, smitten by God, and afflicted. Isaiah 53:4 But he was pierced for our transgressions; he was crushed for our iniquities; upon him was the chastisement that brought us peace, and with his wounds we are healed. Isaiah 53:5 All we like sheep have gone astray; we have turned—every one—to his own way; and the LORD has laid on him the iniquity of us all. Isaiah 53:6 He was oppressed, and he was afflicted, yet he opened not his mouth; like a lamb that is led to the slaughter, and like a sheep that before its shearers is silent, so he opened not his mouth. Isaiah 53:7 By oppression and judgment he was taken away; and as for his generation, who considered that he was cut off out of the land of the living, stricken for the transgression of my people? Isaiah 53:8 And they made his grave with the wicked and with a rich man in his death, although he had done no violence, and there was no deceit in his mouth. Isaiah 53:9 Yet it was the will of the LORD to crush him; he has put him to grief; when his soul makes an offering for guilt, he shall see his offspring; he shall prolong his days; the will of the LORD shall prosper in his hand. Isaiah 53:10 Out of the anguish of his soul he shall see and be satisfied; by his knowledge shall the righteous one, my servant, make many to be accounted righteous, and he shall bear their iniquities. Isaiah 53:11 Therefore I will divide him a portion with the many, and he shall divide the spoil with the strong, because he poured out his soul to death and was numbered with the transgressors; yet he bore the sin of many, and makes intercession for the transgressors. Isaiah 53:12

title: Isaiah 54:1–10
context: After the Servant's guilt offering, Zion is told to sing, O barren one: historic Jerusalem, desolate in exile, shall have more children than the married. Enlarge the tent; offspring will possess the nations and people desolate cities. Fear not: your Maker is your husband, the Holy One of Israel your Redeemer. For a brief moment he deserted her; with everlasting love he will have compassion. This is like the days of Noah: mountains may depart, but his covenant of peace shall not be removed.
text: Isaiah 54:1–10 Isaiah After the Servant's guilt offering, Zion is told to sing, O barren one: historic Jerusalem, desolate in exile, shall have more children than the married. Enlarge the tent; offspring will possess the nations and people desolate cities. Fear not: your Maker is your husband, the Holy One of Israel your Redeemer. For a brief moment he deserted her; with everlasting love he will have compassion. This is like the days of Noah: mountains may depart, but his covenant of peace shall not be removed. "Sing, O barren one, who did not bear; break forth into singing and cry aloud, you who have not been in labor! For the children of the desolate one will be more than the children of her who is married," says the LORD. Isaiah 54:1 "Enlarge the place of your tent, and let the curtains of your habitations be stretched out; do not hold back; lengthen your cords and strengthen your stakes. Isaiah 54:2 For you will spread abroad to the right and to the left, and your offspring will possess the nations and will people the desolate cities. Isaiah 54:3 "Fear not, for you will not be ashamed; be not confounded, for you will not be disgraced; for you will forget the shame of your youth, and the reproach of your widowhood you will remember no more. Isaiah 54:4 For your Maker is your husband, the LORD of hosts is his name; and the Holy One of Israel is your Redeemer, the God of the whole earth he is called. Isaiah 54:5 For the LORD has called you like a wife deserted and grieved in spirit, like a wife of youth when she is cast off, says your God. Isaiah 54:6 For a brief moment I deserted you, but with great compassion I will gather you. Isaiah 54:7 In overflowing anger for a moment I hid my face from you, but with everlasting love I will have compassion on you," says the LORD, your Redeemer. Isaiah 54:8 "This is like the days of Noah to me: as I swore that the waters of Noah should no more go over the earth, so I have sworn that I will not be angry with you, and will not rebuke you. Isaiah 54:9 For the mountains may depart and the hills be removed, but my steadfast love shall not depart from you, and my covenant of peace shall not be removed," says the LORD, who has compassion on you. Isaiah 54:10

title: Isaiah 54:11–17
context: The barren of 54:1–10 is now the storm-tossed city: O afflicted one, not comforted, I will set your stones in antimony and lay your foundations with sapphires. Children taught by the LORD; established in righteousness, far from oppression. If anyone stirs up strife, it is not from me; the smith and the ravager are his creatures. No weapon fashioned against you shall succeed; this is the heritage of the servants of the LORD, their vindication from him. Historic Zion rebuilt after exile, then the gospel church.
text: Isaiah 54:11–17 Isaiah The barren of 54:1–10 is now the storm-tossed city: O afflicted one, not comforted, I will set your stones in antimony and lay your foundations with sapphires. Children taught by the LORD; established in righteousness, far from oppression. If anyone stirs up strife, it is not from me; the smith and the ravager are his creatures. No weapon fashioned against you shall succeed; this is the heritage of the servants of the LORD, their vindication from him. Historic Zion rebuilt after exile, then the gospel church. "O afflicted one, storm-tossed and not comforted, behold, I will set your stones in antimony, and lay your foundations with sapphires. Isaiah 54:11 I will make your pinnacles of agate, your gates of carbuncles, and all your wall of precious stones. Isaiah 54:12 All your children shall be taught by the LORD, and great shall be the peace of your children. Isaiah 54:13 In righteousness you shall be established; you shall be far from oppression, for you shall not fear; and from terror, for it shall not come near you. Isaiah 54:14 If anyone stirs up strife, it is not from me; whoever stirs up strife with you shall fall because of you. Isaiah 54:15 Behold, I have created the smith who blows the fire of coals and produces a weapon for its purpose. I have also created the ravager to destroy; Isaiah 54:16 no weapon that is fashioned against you shall succeed, and you shall refute every tongue that rises against you in judgment. This is the heritage of the servants of the LORD and their vindication from me, declares the LORD." Isaiah 54:17

title: Isaiah 55:1–13
context: After Zion's rebuilt walls, the cry is, Come, everyone who thirsts, come to the waters; buy wine and milk without money. Historic exiles going out in joy, then the gospel: an everlasting covenant, the sure mercies of David, nations running to the Holy One of Israel. Seek the LORD while he may be found; let the wicked forsake his way; my thoughts are not your thoughts. As rain waters the earth, so shall my word accomplish what I purpose. Instead of the thorn, the cypress—an everlasting sign that shall not be cut off. Do not split this invitation.
text: Isaiah 55:1–13 Isaiah After Zion's rebuilt walls, the cry is, Come, everyone who thirsts, come to the waters; buy wine and milk without money. Historic exiles going out in joy, then the gospel: an everlasting covenant, the sure mercies of David, nations running to the Holy One of Israel. Seek the LORD while he may be found; let the wicked forsake his way; my thoughts are not your thoughts. As rain waters the earth, so shall my word accomplish what I purpose. Instead of the thorn, the cypress—an everlasting sign that shall not be cut off. Do not split this invitation. "Come, everyone who thirsts, come to the waters; and he who has no money, come, buy and eat! Come, buy wine and milk without money and without price. Isaiah 55:1 Why do you spend your money for that which is not bread, and your labor for that which does not satisfy? Listen diligently to me, and eat what is good, and delight yourselves in rich food. Isaiah 55:2 Incline your ear, and come to me; hear, that your soul may live; and I will make with you an everlasting covenant, my steadfast, sure love for David. Isaiah 55:3 Behold, I made him a witness to the peoples, a leader and commander for the peoples. Isaiah 55:4 Behold, you shall call a nation that you do not know, and a nation that did not know you shall run to you, because of the LORD your God, and of the Holy One of Israel, for he has glorified you. Isaiah 55:5 "Seek the LORD while he may be found; call upon him while he is near; Isaiah 55:6 let the wicked forsake his way, and the unrighteous man his thoughts; let him return to the LORD, that he may have compassion on him, and to our God, for he will abundantly pardon. Isaiah 55:7 For my thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways, declares the LORD. Isaiah 55:8 For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways and my thoughts than your thoughts. Isaiah 55:9 "For as the rain and the snow come down from heaven and do not return there but water the earth, making it bring forth and sprout, giving seed to the sower and bread to the eater, Isaiah 55:10 so shall my word be that goes out from my mouth; it shall not return to me empty, but it shall accomplish that which I purpose, and shall succeed in the thing for which I sent it. Isaiah 55:11 "For you shall go out with joy and be led forth in peace; the mountains and the hills before you shall break forth into singing, and all the trees of the field shall clap their hands. Isaiah 55:12 Instead of the thorn shall come up the cypress; instead of the brier shall come up the myrtle; and it shall make a name for the LORD, an everlasting sign that shall not be cut off." Isaiah 55:13

title: Isaiah 56:1–8
context: After the Servant’s work and the free invitation of chapter 55, the Lord commands justice and righteousness because his salvation is near. Foreigners and eunuchs who hold the covenant are promised a name in his house; the mountain becomes a house of prayer for all peoples, and the God who gathers Israel’s outcasts will gather still others.
text: Isaiah 56:1–8 Isaiah After the Servant’s work and the free invitation of chapter 55, the Lord commands justice and righteousness because his salvation is near. Foreigners and eunuchs who hold the covenant are promised a name in his house; the mountain becomes a house of prayer for all peoples, and the God who gathers Israel’s outcasts will gather still others. Thus says the Lord: “Keep justice, and do righteousness, for soon my salvation will come, and my righteousness be revealed. Isaiah 56:1 Blessed is the man who does this, and the son of man who holds it fast, who keeps the Sabbath, not profaning it, and keeps his hand from doing any evil.” Isaiah 56:2 Let not the foreigner who has joined himself to the Lord say, “The Lord will surely separate me from his people”; and let not the eunuch say, “Behold, I am a dry tree.” Isaiah 56:3 For thus says the Lord: “To the eunuchs who keep my Sabbaths, who choose the things that please me and hold fast my covenant, Isaiah 56:4 I will give in my house and within my walls a monument and a name better than sons and daughters; I will give them an everlasting name that shall not be cut off. Isaiah 56:5 “And the foreigners who join themselves to the Lord, to minister to him, to love the name of the Lord, and to be his servants, everyone who keeps the Sabbath and does not profane it, and holds fast my covenant— Isaiah 56:6 these I will bring to my holy mountain, and make them joyful in my house of prayer; their burnt offerings and their sacrifices will be accepted on my altar; for my house shall be called a house of prayer for all peoples.” Isaiah 56:7 The Lord God, who gathers the outcasts of Israel, declares, “I will gather yet others to him besides those already gathered.” Isaiah 56:8

title: Isaiah 56:9–12
context: The welcome of foreigners and eunuchs turns to a summons of wild beasts against a people whose watchmen are blind. Priests and shepherds sleep, crave, and toast tomorrow, while the flock is left to be devoured.
text: Isaiah 56:9–12 Isaiah The welcome of foreigners and eunuchs turns to a summons of wild beasts against a people whose watchmen are blind. Priests and shepherds sleep, crave, and toast tomorrow, while the flock is left to be devoured. All you beasts of the field, come to devour— all you beasts in the forest. Isaiah 56:9 His watchmen are blind; they are all without knowledge; they are all silent dogs; they cannot bark, dreaming, lying down, loving to slumber. Isaiah 56:10 The dogs have a mighty appetite; they never have enough. But they are shepherds who have no understanding; they have all turned to their own way, each to his own gain, one and all. Isaiah 56:11 “Come,” they say, “let me get wine; let us fill ourselves with strong drink; and tomorrow will be like this day, great beyond measure.” Isaiah 56:12

title: Isaiah 57:1–13
context: While drunk watchmen sleep, the righteous perish and enter peace. The Lord then summons a people of sorcery and spiritual adultery: child-sacrifice in the valleys, beds on high places, envoys to a foreign king even to Sheol. Idols will not profit; the one who takes refuge in the Lord shall possess the land and inherit the holy mountain.
text: Isaiah 57:1–13 Isaiah While drunk watchmen sleep, the righteous perish and enter peace. The Lord then summons a people of sorcery and spiritual adultery: child-sacrifice in the valleys, beds on high places, envoys to a foreign king even to Sheol. Idols will not profit; the one who takes refuge in the Lord shall possess the land and inherit the holy mountain. The righteous man perishes, and no one lays it to heart; devout men are taken away, while no one understands. For the righteous man is taken away from calamity; Isaiah 57:1 he enters into peace; they rest in their beds who walk in their uprightness. Isaiah 57:2 But you, draw near, sons of the sorceress, offspring of the adulterer and the loose woman. Isaiah 57:3 Whom are you mocking? Against whom do you open your mouth wide and stick out your tongue? Are you not children of transgression, the offspring of deceit, Isaiah 57:4 you who burn with lust among the oaks, under every green tree, who slaughter your children in the valleys, under the clefts of the rocks? Isaiah 57:5 Among the smooth stones of the valley is your portion; they, they, are your lot; to them you have poured out a drink offering, you have brought a grain offering. Shall I relent for these things? Isaiah 57:6 On a high and lofty mountain you have set your bed, and there you went up to offer sacrifice. Isaiah 57:7 Behind the door and the doorpost you have set up your memorial; for, deserting me, you have uncovered your bed, you have gone up to it, you have made it wide; and you have made a covenant for yourself with them, you have loved their bed, you have looked on nakedness. Isaiah 57:8 You journeyed to the king with oil and multiplied your perfumes; you sent your envoys far off, and sent down even to Sheol. Isaiah 57:9 You were wearied with the length of your way, but you did not say, “It is hopeless”; you found new life for your strength, and so you were not faint. Isaiah 57:10 Whom did you dread and fear, so that you lied, and did not remember me, did not lay it to heart? Have I not held my peace, even for a long time, and you do not fear me? Isaiah 57:11 I will declare your righteousness and your deeds, but they will not profit you. Isaiah 57:12 When you cry out, let your collection of idols deliver you! The wind will carry them all off, a breath will take them away. But he who takes refuge in me shall possess the land and shall inherit my holy mountain.” Isaiah 57:13

title: Isaiah 57:14–21
context: After the idolatry of 57:1–13, a voice commands the way to be built up. The High and Holy One dwells with the contrite, will not contend forever, heals the backslider, and creates “Peace, peace” for the far and the near. The wicked remain a tossing sea: no peace for them.
text: Isaiah 57:14–21 Isaiah After the idolatry of 57:1–13, a voice commands the way to be built up. The High and Holy One dwells with the contrite, will not contend forever, heals the backslider, and creates “Peace, peace” for the far and the near. The wicked remain a tossing sea: no peace for them. And it shall be said, “Build up, build up, prepare the way, remove every obstruction from my people's way.” Isaiah 57:14 For thus says the One who is high and lifted up, who inhabits eternity, whose name is Holy: “I dwell in the high and holy place, and also with him who is of a contrite and lowly spirit, to revive the spirit of the lowly, and to revive the heart of the contrite. Isaiah 57:15 For I will not contend forever, nor will I always be angry; for the spirit would grow faint before me, and the breath of life that I made. Isaiah 57:16 Because of the iniquity of his unjust gain I was angry, I struck him; I hid my face and was angry, but he went on backsliding in the way of his own heart. Isaiah 57:17 I have seen his ways, but I will heal him; I will lead him and restore comfort to him and his mourners, Isaiah 57:18 creating the fruit of the lips. Peace, peace, to the far and to the near,” says the Lord, “and I will heal him. Isaiah 57:19 But the wicked are like the tossing sea; for it cannot be quiet, and its waters toss up mire and dirt. Isaiah 57:20 There is no peace,” says my God, “for the wicked.” Isaiah 57:21

title: Isaiah 58:1–14
context: The Lord commands a trumpet cry against Jacob’s sin. Daily seeking and fasting are unmasked: pleasure, oppression, quarreling. The fast he chooses looses yokes, shares bread, houses the poor, and honors the Sabbath. Then light, healing, rebuilt ruins, and the heritage of Jacob follow, for the mouth of the Lord has spoken.
text: Isaiah 58:1–14 Isaiah The Lord commands a trumpet cry against Jacob’s sin. Daily seeking and fasting are unmasked: pleasure, oppression, quarreling. The fast he chooses looses yokes, shares bread, houses the poor, and honors the Sabbath. Then light, healing, rebuilt ruins, and the heritage of Jacob follow, for the mouth of the Lord has spoken. “Cry aloud; do not hold back; lift up your voice like a trumpet; declare to my people their transgression, to the house of Jacob their sins. Isaiah 58:1 Yet they seek me daily and delight to know my ways, as if they were a nation that did righteousness and did not forsake the judgment of their God; they ask of me righteous judgments; they delight to draw near to God. Isaiah 58:2 ‘Why have we fasted, and you see it not? Why have we humbled ourselves, and you take no knowledge of it?’ Behold, in the day of your fast you seek your own pleasure, and oppress all your workers. Isaiah 58:3 Behold, you fast only to quarrel and to fight and to hit with a wicked fist. Fasting like yours this day will not make your voice to be heard on high. Isaiah 58:4 Is such the fast that I choose, a day for a person to humble himself? Is it to bow down his head like a reed, and to spread sackcloth and ashes under him? Will you call this a fast, and a day acceptable to the Lord? Isaiah 58:5 “Is not this the fast that I choose: to loose the bonds of wickedness, to undo the straps of the yoke, to let the oppressed go free, and to break every yoke? Isaiah 58:6 Is it not to share your bread with the hungry and bring the homeless poor into your house; when you see the naked, to cover him, and not to hide yourself from your own flesh? Isaiah 58:7 Then shall your light break forth like the dawn, and your healing shall spring up speedily; your righteousness shall go before you; the glory of the Lord shall be your rear guard. Isaiah 58:8 Then you shall call, and the Lord will answer; you shall cry, and he will say, ‘Here I am.’ If you take away the yoke from your midst, the pointing of the finger, and speaking wickedness, Isaiah 58:9 if you pour yourself out for the hungry and satisfy the desire of the afflicted, then shall your light rise in the darkness and your gloom be as the noonday. Isaiah 58:10 And the Lord will guide you continually and satisfy your desire in scorched places and make your bones strong; and you shall be like a watered garden, like a spring of water, whose waters do not fail. Isaiah 58:11 And your ancient ruins shall be rebuilt; you shall raise up the foundations of many generations; you shall be called the repairer of the breach, the restorer of streets to dwell in. Isaiah 58:12 “If you turn back your foot from the Sabbath, from doing your pleasure on my holy day, and call the Sabbath a delight and the holy day of the Lord honorable; if you honor it, not going your own ways, or seeking your own pleasure, or talking idly; Isaiah 58:13 then you shall take delight in the Lord, and I will make you ride on the heights of the earth; I will feed you with the heritage of Jacob your father, for the mouth of the Lord has spoken.” Isaiah 58:14

title: Isaiah 59:1–13
context: The Lord’s hand is not too short to save, nor his ear too dull to hear. Iniquity has made the separation: bloodied hands, lying lips, adder eggs, crooked roads with no peace. The people then confess: we grope like the blind, hope for justice and find none, because our transgressions are multiplied and we know our iniquities.
text: Isaiah 59:1–13 Isaiah The Lord’s hand is not too short to save, nor his ear too dull to hear. Iniquity has made the separation: bloodied hands, lying lips, adder eggs, crooked roads with no peace. The people then confess: we grope like the blind, hope for justice and find none, because our transgressions are multiplied and we know our iniquities. Behold, the Lord's hand is not shortened, that it cannot save, or his ear dull, that it cannot hear; Isaiah 59:1 but your iniquities have made a separation between you and your God, and your sins have hidden his face from you so that he does not hear. Isaiah 59:2 For your hands are defiled with blood and your fingers with iniquity; your lips have spoken lies; your tongue mutters wickedness. Isaiah 59:3 No one enters suit justly; no one goes to law honestly; they rely on empty pleas, they speak lies, they conceive mischief and give birth to iniquity. Isaiah 59:4 They hatch adders' eggs; they weave the spider's web; he who eats their eggs dies, and from one that is crushed a viper is hatched. Isaiah 59:5 Their webs will not serve as clothing; men will not cover themselves with what they make. Their works are works of iniquity, and deeds of violence are in their hands. Isaiah 59:6 Their feet run to evil, and they are swift to shed innocent blood; their thoughts are thoughts of iniquity; desolation and destruction are in their highways. Isaiah 59:7 The way of peace they do not know, and there is no justice in their paths; they have made their roads crooked; no one who treads on them knows peace. Isaiah 59:8 Therefore justice is far from us, and righteousness does not overtake us; we hope for light, and behold, darkness, and for brightness, but we walk in gloom. Isaiah 59:9 We grope for the wall like the blind; we grope like those who have no eyes; we stumble at noon as in the twilight, among those in full vigor we are like dead men. Isaiah 59:10 We all growl like bears; we moan and moan like doves; we hope for justice, but there is none; for salvation, but it is far from us. Isaiah 59:11 For our transgressions are multiplied before you, and our sins testify against us; for our transgressions are with us, and we know our iniquities: Isaiah 59:12 transgressing, and denying the Lord, and turning back from following our God, speaking oppression and revolt, conceiving and uttering from the heart lying words. Isaiah 59:13

title: Isaiah 59:14–21
context: After the confession of 59:1–13, justice is turned back in the square and the one who departs from evil becomes a prey. The Lord sees there is no intercessor; his own arm brings salvation. A Redeemer comes to Zion, to those in Jacob who turn from transgression, and the covenant of Spirit and word will not depart from their mouth forever.
text: Isaiah 59:14–21 Isaiah After the confession of 59:1–13, justice is turned back in the square and the one who departs from evil becomes a prey. The Lord sees there is no intercessor; his own arm brings salvation. A Redeemer comes to Zion, to those in Jacob who turn from transgression, and the covenant of Spirit and word will not depart from their mouth forever. Justice is turned back, and righteousness stands far away; for truth has stumbled in the public squares, and uprightness cannot enter. Isaiah 59:14 Truth is lacking, and he who departs from evil makes himself a prey. The Lord saw it, and it displeased him that there was no justice. Isaiah 59:15 He saw that there was no man, and wondered that there was no one to intercede; then his own arm brought him salvation, and his righteousness upheld him. Isaiah 59:16 He put on righteousness as a breastplate, and a helmet of salvation on his head; he put on garments of vengeance for clothing, and wrapped himself in zeal as a cloak. Isaiah 59:17 According to their deeds, so will he repay, wrath to his adversaries, repayment to his enemies; to the coastlands he will render repayment. Isaiah 59:18 So they shall fear the name of the Lord from the west, and his glory from the rising of the sun; for he will come like a rushing stream, which the wind of the Lord drives. Isaiah 59:19 “And a Redeemer will come to Zion, to those in Jacob who turn from transgression,” declares the Lord. Isaiah 59:20 “And as for me, this is my covenant with them,” says the Lord: “My Spirit that is upon you, and my words that I have put in your mouth, shall not depart out of your mouth, or out of the mouth of your offspring, or out of the mouth of your children's offspring,” says the Lord, “from this time forth and forevermore.” Isaiah 59:21

title: Isaiah 6:1–13
context: In the year King Uzziah died, Isaiah sees the Lord on a throne, high and lifted up; seraphim cry Holy, holy, holy. Thresholds shake; the house fills with smoke. Woe is me—unclean lips among an unclean people. A coal from the altar touches his mouth: guilt taken away, sin atoned. Whom shall I send, who will go for us? Here am I. Go: keep hearing, do not understand; make the heart dull, lest they turn and be healed. How long? Until cities lie waste. A tenth remains and is burned again; the holy seed is the stump.
text: Isaiah 6:1–13 Isaiah In the year King Uzziah died, Isaiah sees the Lord on a throne, high and lifted up; seraphim cry Holy, holy, holy. Thresholds shake; the house fills with smoke. Woe is me—unclean lips among an unclean people. A coal from the altar touches his mouth: guilt taken away, sin atoned. Whom shall I send, who will go for us? Here am I. Go: keep hearing, do not understand; make the heart dull, lest they turn and be healed. How long? Until cities lie waste. A tenth remains and is burned again; the holy seed is the stump. In the year that King Uzziah died I saw the Lord sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up; and the train of his robe filled the temple. Isaiah 6:1 Above him stood the seraphim. Each had six wings: with two he covered his face, and with two he covered his feet, and with two he flew. Isaiah 6:2 And one called to another and said: “Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of hosts; the whole earth is full of his glory!” Isaiah 6:3 And the foundations of the thresholds shook at the voice of him who called, and the house was filled with smoke. Isaiah 6:4 And I said: “Woe is me! For I am lost; for I am a man of unclean lips, and I dwell in the midst of a people of unclean lips; for my eyes have seen the King, the Lord of hosts!” Isaiah 6:5 Then one of the seraphim flew to me, having in his hand a burning coal that he had taken with tongs from the altar. Isaiah 6:6 And he touched my mouth and said: “Behold, this has touched your lips; your guilt is taken away, and your sin atoned for.” Isaiah 6:7 And I heard the voice of the Lord saying, “Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” Then I said, “Here I am! Send me.” Isaiah 6:8 And he said, “Go, and say to this people: “‘Keep on hearing, but do not understand; keep on seeing, but do not perceive.’ Isaiah 6:9 Make the heart of this people dull, and their ears heavy, and blind their eyes; lest they see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their hearts, and turn and be healed.” Isaiah 6:10 Then I said, “How long, O Lord?” And he said: “Until cities lie waste without inhabitant, and houses without people, and the land is a desolate waste, Isaiah 6:11 and the Lord removes people far away, and the forsaken places are many in the midst of the land. Isaiah 6:12 And though a tenth remain in it, it will be burned again, like a terebinth or an oak, whose stump remains when it is felled.” The holy seed is its stump. Isaiah 6:13

title: Isaiah 60:1–9
context: After the Redeemer of 59:20, Zion is told to arise: the Lord’s glory has risen, while darkness covers the peoples. Nations and kings come to her light; sons and daughters return; sea-wealth, Midian’s camels, Sheba’s gold and frankincense, Kedar’s flocks, and Tarshish ships bring children and praise to the Holy One who has made her beautiful.
text: Isaiah 60:1–9 Isaiah After the Redeemer of 59:20, Zion is told to arise: the Lord’s glory has risen, while darkness covers the peoples. Nations and kings come to her light; sons and daughters return; sea-wealth, Midian’s camels, Sheba’s gold and frankincense, Kedar’s flocks, and Tarshish ships bring children and praise to the Holy One who has made her beautiful. Arise, shine, for your light has come, and the glory of the Lord has risen upon you. Isaiah 60:1 For behold, darkness shall cover the earth, and thick darkness the peoples; but the Lord will arise upon you, and his glory will be seen upon you. Isaiah 60:2 And nations shall come to your light, and kings to the brightness of your rising. Isaiah 60:3 Lift up your eyes all around, and see; they all gather together, they come to you; your sons shall come from afar, and your daughters shall be carried on the hip. Isaiah 60:4 Then you shall see and be radiant; your heart shall thrill and exult, because the abundance of the sea shall be turned to you, the wealth of the nations shall come to you. Isaiah 60:5 A multitude of camels shall cover you, the young camels of Midian and Ephah; all those from Sheba shall come. They shall bring gold and frankincense, and shall bring good news, the praises of the Lord. Isaiah 60:6 All the flocks of Kedar shall be gathered to you; the rams of Nebaioth shall minister to you; they shall come up with acceptance on my altar, and I will beautify my beautiful house. Isaiah 60:7 Who are these that fly like a cloud, and like doves to their windows? Isaiah 60:8 For the coastlands shall hope for me, the ships of Tarshish first, to bring your children from afar, their silver and gold with them, for the name of the Lord your God, and for the Holy One of Israel, because he has made you beautiful. Isaiah 60:9

title: Isaiah 60:10–22
context: Foreigners build Zion’s walls and kings minister, after wrath, in favor. Gates stay open for the nations’ wealth; Lebanon beautifies the sanctuary; afflicters bow and name her the City of the Lord. God himself is everlasting light. The people are his planting, and he will hasten it in its time.
text: Isaiah 60:10–22 Isaiah Foreigners build Zion’s walls and kings minister, after wrath, in favor. Gates stay open for the nations’ wealth; Lebanon beautifies the sanctuary; afflicters bow and name her the City of the Lord. God himself is everlasting light. The people are his planting, and he will hasten it in its time. Foreigners shall build up your walls, and their kings shall minister to you; for in my wrath I struck you, but in my favor I have had mercy on you. Isaiah 60:10 Your gates shall be open continually; day and night they shall not be shut, that people may bring to you the wealth of the nations, with their kings led in procession. Isaiah 60:11 For the nation and kingdom that will not serve you shall perish; those nations shall be utterly laid waste. Isaiah 60:12 The glory of Lebanon shall come to you, the cypress, the plane, and the pine, to beautify the place of my sanctuary, and I will make the place of my feet glorious. Isaiah 60:13 The sons of those who afflicted you shall come bending low to you, and all who despised you shall bow down at your feet; they shall call you the City of the Lord, the Zion of the Holy One of Israel. Isaiah 60:14 Whereas you have been forsaken and hated, with no one passing through, I will make you majestic forever, a joy from age to age. Isaiah 60:15 You shall suck the milk of nations; you shall nurse at the breast of kings; and you shall know that I, the Lord, am your Savior and your Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob. Isaiah 60:16 Instead of bronze I will bring gold, and instead of iron I will bring silver; instead of wood, bronze, instead of stones, iron. I will make your overseers peace and your taskmasters righteousness. Isaiah 60:17 Violence shall no more be heard in your land, devastation or destruction within your borders; you shall call your walls Salvation, and your gates Praise. Isaiah 60:18 The sun shall be no more your light by day, nor for brightness shall the moon give you light; but the Lord will be your everlasting light, and your God will be your glory. Isaiah 60:19 Your sun shall no more go down, nor your moon withdraw itself; for the Lord will be your everlasting light, and your days of mourning shall be ended. Isaiah 60:20 Your people shall all be righteous; they shall possess the land forever, the branch of my planting, the work of my hands, that I might be glorified. Isaiah 60:21 The least one shall become a clan, and the smallest one a mighty nation; I am the Lord; in its time I will hasten it. Isaiah 60:22

title: Isaiah 61:1–11
context: The anointed Servant brings good news, liberty, and the year of the Lord’s favor with a day of vengeance, to comfort Zion’s mourners. Ruins rise; strangers tend flocks; the people are named priests under an everlasting covenant. Garments of salvation clothe the church. Jesus reads 61:1–2 at Nazareth (Luke 4:16–21).
text: Isaiah 61:1–11 Isaiah The anointed Servant brings good news, liberty, and the year of the Lord’s favor with a day of vengeance, to comfort Zion’s mourners. Ruins rise; strangers tend flocks; the people are named priests under an everlasting covenant. Garments of salvation clothe the church. Jesus reads 61:1–2 at Nazareth (Luke 4:16–21). The Spirit of the Lord God is upon me, because the Lord has anointed me to bring good news to the poor; he has sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and the opening of the prison to those who are bound; Isaiah 61:1 to proclaim the year of the Lord’s favor, and the day of vengeance of our God; to comfort all who mourn; Isaiah 61:2 to grant to those who mourn in Zion—to give them a beautiful headdress instead of ashes, the oil of gladness instead of mourning, the garment of praise instead of a faint spirit; that they may be called oaks of righteousness, the planting of the Lord, that he may be glorified. Isaiah 61:3 They shall build up the ancient ruins; they shall raise up the former devastations; they shall repair the ruined cities, the devastations of many generations. Isaiah 61:4 Strangers shall stand and tend your flocks; foreigners shall be your plowmen and vinedressers; Isaiah 61:5 but you shall be called the priests of the Lord; they shall speak of you as the ministers of our God; you shall eat the wealth of the nations, and in their glory you shall boast. Isaiah 61:6 Instead of your shame there shall be a double portion; instead of dishonor they shall rejoice in their lot; therefore in their land they shall possess a double portion; they shall have everlasting joy. Isaiah 61:7 For I the Lord love justice; I hate robbery and wrong; I will faithfully give them their recompense, and I will make an everlasting covenant with them. Isaiah 61:8 Their offspring shall be known among the nations, and their descendants in the midst of the peoples; all who see them shall acknowledge them, that they are an offspring the Lord has blessed. Isaiah 61:9 I will greatly rejoice in the Lord; my soul shall exult in my God, for he has clothed me with the garments of salvation; he has covered me with the robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom decks himself like a priest with a beautiful headdress, and as a bride adorns herself with her jewels. Isaiah 61:10 For as the earth brings forth its sprouts, and as a garden causes what is sown in it to sprout up, so the Lord God will cause righteousness and praise to sprout up before all the nations. Isaiah 61:11

title: Isaiah 62:1–12
context: The prophet will not keep silent until Zion’s righteousness shines and her salvation burns like a torch. Forsaken names are changed: Hephzibah, Beulah; watchmen take no rest; a highway is cleared; the Holy People are Sought Out, A City Not Forsaken. Historic restoration after exile comes first; the church is the same people under the gospel. Bridegroom joy and a sworn harvest belong to that one story—not a newspaper, not a millennial chart.
text: Isaiah 62:1–12 Isaiah The prophet will not keep silent until Zion’s righteousness shines and her salvation burns like a torch. Forsaken names are changed: Hephzibah, Beulah; watchmen take no rest; a highway is cleared; the Holy People are Sought Out, A City Not Forsaken. Historic restoration after exile comes first; the church is the same people under the gospel. Bridegroom joy and a sworn harvest belong to that one story—not a newspaper, not a millennial chart. For Zion’s sake I will not keep silent, and for Jerusalem’s sake I will not be quiet, until her righteousness goes forth as brightness, and her salvation as a burning torch. Isaiah 62:1 The nations shall see your righteousness, and all the kings your glory, and you shall be called by a new name that the mouth of the Lord will give. Isaiah 62:2 You shall be a crown of beauty in the hand of the Lord, and a royal diadem in the hand of your God. Isaiah 62:3 You shall no more be termed Forsaken, and your land shall no more be termed Desolate, but you shall be called My Delight Is in Her, and your land Married; for the Lord delights in you, and your land shall be married. Isaiah 62:4 For as a young man marries a young woman, so shall your sons marry you, and as the bridegroom rejoices over the bride, so shall your God rejoice over you. Isaiah 62:5 On your walls, O Jerusalem, I have set watchmen; all the day and all the night they shall never be silent. You who put the Lord in remembrance, take no rest, Isaiah 62:6 and give him no rest until he establishes Jerusalem and makes it a praise in the earth. Isaiah 62:7 The Lord has sworn by his right hand and by his mighty arm: "I will not again give your grain to be food for your enemies, and foreigners shall not drink your wine for which you have labored; Isaiah 62:8 but those who garner it shall eat it and praise the Lord, and those who gather it shall drink it in the courts of my sanctuary." Isaiah 62:9 Go through, go through the gates; prepare the way for the people; build up, build up the highway; clear it of stones; lift up a signal over the peoples. Isaiah 62:10 Behold, the Lord has proclaimed to the end of the earth: Say to the daughter of Zion, "Behold, your salvation comes; behold, his reward is with him, and his recompense before him." Isaiah 62:11 And they shall be called The Holy People, The Redeemed of the Lord; and you shall be called Sought Out, A City Not Forsaken. Isaiah 62:12

Isaiah 64:5 We have all become like one who is unclean, and all our righteous deeds are like a polluted garment. We all fade like a leaf, and our iniquities, like the wind, take us away. Isaiah 64:6 There is no one who calls upon your name, who rouses himself to take hold of you; for you have hidden your face from us, and have made us melt in the hand of our iniquities. Isaiah 64:7 But now, O Lord, you are our Father; we are the clay, and you are our potter; we are all the work of your hand. title: Isaiah 65:1–16

text: Isaiah 65:1–16 Isaiah The Lord answers the plea of chapters 63–64. He was ready to be found by a nation not called by his name; he spread out his hands all day to a rebellious people who sacrificed in gardens, sat in tombs, and said, Keep to yourself. Yet as new wine in the cluster, he will not destroy them all: offspring from Jacob, chosen servants on the mountains, Sharon and Achor for those who sought him. Fortune and Destiny get a sword; servants eat and drink. Historic Judah and the nations first, then the gospel Paul reads here (Rom 10:20–21)—not a newspaper and not a millennial camp fight. I was ready to be sought by those who did not ask for me; I was ready to be found by those who did not seek me. I said, "Here I am, here I am," to a nation that was not called by my name. Isaiah 65:1 I spread out my hands all the day to a rebellious people, who walk in a way that is not good, following their own devices; Isaiah 65:2 a people who provoke me to my face continually, sacrificing in gardens and making offerings on bricks; Isaiah 65:3 who sit in tombs, and spend the night in secret places; who eat pig's flesh, and broth of tainted meat is in their vessels; Isaiah 65:4 who say, "Keep to yourself, do not come near me, for I am too holy for you." These are a smoke in my nostrils, a fire that burns all the day. Isaiah 65:5 Behold, it is written before me: "I will not keep silent, but I will repay; I will indeed repay into their lap Isaiah 65:6 both your iniquities and your fathers' iniquities together, says the Lord; because they made offerings on the mountains and insulted me on the hills, I will measure into their lap payment for their former deeds." Isaiah 65:7 Thus says the Lord: "As the new wine is found in the cluster, and they say, 'Do not destroy it, for there is a blessing in it,' so I will do for my servants' sake, and not destroy them all. Isaiah 65:8 I will bring forth offspring from Jacob, and from Judah possessors of my mountains; my chosen shall possess it, and my servants shall dwell there. Isaiah 65:9 Sharon shall become a pasture for flocks, and the Valley of Achor a place for herds to lie down, for my people who have sought me. Isaiah 65:10 But you who forsake the Lord, who forget my holy mountain, who set a table for Fortune and fill cups of mixed wine for Destiny, Isaiah 65:11 I will destine you to the sword, and all of you shall bow down to the slaughter, because, when I called, you did not answer; when I spoke, you did not listen, but you did what was evil in my eyes and chose what I did not delight in." Isaiah 65:12 Therefore thus says the Lord God: "Behold, my servants shall eat, but you shall be hungry; behold, my servants shall drink, but you shall be thirsty; behold, my servants shall rejoice, but you shall be put to shame; Isaiah 65:13 behold, my servants shall sing for gladness of heart, but you shall cry out for pain of heart and shall wail for breaking of spirit. Isaiah 65:14 You shall leave your name to my chosen for a curse, and the Lord God will put you to death, but his servants he will call by another name, Isaiah 65:15 so that he who blesses himself in the land shall bless himself by the God of truth, and he who takes an oath in the land shall swear by the God of truth; because the former troubles are forgotten and are hidden from my eyes." Isaiah 65:16

title: Isaiah 65:17–25
context: After the servants’ new name, the Lord creates new heavens and a new earth; former troubles are not remembered. Jerusalem is created a joy; no more weeping; long life; houses built and inhabited; they call and he answers; wolf and lamb graze together; they shall not hurt in all my holy mountain. Historic Zion after exile comes first; then the gospel church and the last renewal in Christ. This is not a newspaper, and not an Arminian-versus-Reformed millennial camp fight. Wesley and Calvin both read a new face on the world in the Messiah’s kingdom; they do not chart a thousand years against each other.

Isaiah 65:18 I will rejoice in Jerusalem and be glad in my people; no more shall be heard in it the sound of weeping and the cry of distress. Isaiah 65:19 No more shall there be in it an infant who lives but a few days, or an old man who does not fill out his days, for the young man shall die a hundred years old, and the sinner a hundred years old shall be accursed. Isaiah 65:20 They shall build houses and inhabit them; they shall plant vineyards and eat their fruit. Isaiah 65:23 Before they call I will answer; while they are yet speaking I will hear. These have chosen their own ways, and their soul delights in their abominations; Isaiah 66:3 I also will choose harsh treatment for them and bring their fears upon them, because when I called, no one answered, when I spoke, they did not listen; but they did what was evil in my eyes and chose that in which I did not delight." Isaiah 66:4 Hear the word of the Lord, you who tremble at his word: "Your brothers who hate you and cast you out for my name's sake have said, 'Let the Lord be glorified, that we may see your joy'; but it is they who shall be put to shame. Isaiah 66:19 And they shall bring all your brothers from all the nations as an offering to the Lord, on horses and in chariots and in litters and on mules and on dromedaries, to my holy mountain Jerusalem, says the Lord, just as the Israelites bring their grain offering in a clean vessel to the house of the Lord. Isaiah 66:20 And some of them also I will take for priests and for Levites, says the Lord. Isaiah 66:21 "For as the new heavens and the new earth that I make shall remain before me, says the Lord, so shall your offspring and your name remain. title: Isaiah 66:7–14
context: Before Zion is in labor she gives birth; a land is born in a day; the Lord who brings to birth will not shut the womb.
